```ts
// When Pro ends (spec "2. Pro", Server; Review Focus 1 and 2): an annual grant's expires_at is the
// expiration_at_ms of the latest grant, CANCELLATION, or SUBSCRIPTION_EXTENDED event by
// event_timestamp_ms; a lifetime grant has none. A refund (a CUSTOMER_SUPPORT CANCELLATION) revokes
// and keeps the expiry the grant set. An annual grant without expiration_at_ms fails closed: it is recorded and
// answered 200, grants nothing, moves no expiry, and logs one warning. A revoke keeps expires_at
// as it was, so a RENEWAL stamped before a recorded EXPIRATION neither re-grants nor moves
// expires_at forward. Any other annual CANCELLATION never changes the status. The annual and lifetime rows are
// independent, so an annual EXPIRATION never touches a lifetime grant.
import { randomBytes, randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';

import request from 'supertest';
import { afterAll, beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, inject, it } from 'vitest';

import { createMigratedDatabase } from '../integration/createMigratedDatabase.js';
import { createWebhookTestApp } from '../integration/createWebhookTestApp.js';
import { SKIP_DATABASE_TESTS } from '../integration/skipDatabaseTests.js';

const ROUTE = '/v1/webhooks/revenuecat';
const SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000;
const DISTINCTIVE_BYTES = 12;
const T0 = 1_790_000_000_000;
const HOUR_MS = 3_600_000;
const DAY_MS = 86_400_000;
const YEAR_MS = 31_536_000_000;
const FIRST_PERIOD_END = T0 + YEAR_MS;
const SECOND_PERIOD_END = T0 + 2 * YEAR_MS;
const PINO_WARN_LEVEL = 40;
const ANNUAL = 'syntactical.pro.annual';
const LIFETIME = 'syntactical.pro.lifetime';

let database: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof createMigratedDatabase>>;

type TestApp = ReturnType<typeof createWebhookTestApp>['app'];

interface Target {
  app: TestApp;
  logLines: string[];
  revenueCatAuth: string;
  userId: string;
}

interface RowState {
  expiresAtMs: number | null;
  status: string;
}

function buildEvent(overrides: Record<string, unknown>): Record<string, unknown> {
  return {
    app_user_id: randomUUID(),
    environment: 'SANDBOX',
    event_timestamp_ms: T0,
    id: randomUUID(),
    product_id: ANNUAL,
    store: 'APP_STORE',
    transaction_id: randomBytes(DISTINCTIVE_BYTES).toString('hex'),
    type: 'INITIAL_PURCHASE',
    ...overrides,
  };
}

async function setup(): Promise<Target> {
  const { app, logLines, revenueCatAuth } = createWebhookTestApp({ pool: database.pool });
  const { rows } = await database.pool.query<{ id: string }>('INSERT INTO users (email) VALUES ($1) RETURNING id', [
    `learner-${randomUUID()}@example.com`,
  ]);
  return { app, logLines, revenueCatAuth, userId: rows[0].id };
}

function flushLogs(): Promise<void> {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    setImmediate(resolve);
  });
}

async function deliver(target: Target, overrides: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void> {
  const response = await request(target.app)
    .post(ROUTE)
    .set('Authorization', target.revenueCatAuth)
    .set('Content-Type', 'application/json')
    .send(JSON.stringify({ event: buildEvent({ app_user_id: target.userId, ...overrides }) }));
  expect(response.body).toEqual({ data: { status: 'recorded' } });
}

function annual(type: string, at: number, expirationAtMs?: number): Record<string, unknown> {
  return { event_timestamp_ms: at, expiration_at_ms: expirationAtMs, product_id: ANNUAL, type };
}

function lifetime(type: string, at: number): Record<string, unknown> {
  return { event_timestamp_ms: at, product_id: LIFETIME, type };
}

async function rowOf(userId: string, productId: string): Promise<RowState | undefined> {
  const { rows } = await database.pool.query<{ expires_at: Date | null; status: string }>(
    'SELECT status, expires_at FROM entitlements WHERE user_id = $1 AND product_id = $2',
    [userId, productId],
  );
  const [row] = rows;
  return row ? { expiresAtMs: row.expires_at?.getTime() ?? null, status: row.status } : undefined;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

`server/src/services/recomputeEntitlement.ts`, replaced whole:

```ts
// Sets the (user, Pro product) entitlement from the purchase events of the stores that can change
// it. Status: the latest grant or revoke event by occurred_at wins, a revoke winning a tie. What
// revokes comes from the product's rule (PRO_PRODUCT_RULES): a REVOKE_TYPES event always; a
// CANCELLATION when the product's cancellation is 'revoke' (the lifetime product); and, on either
// product, a CANCELLATION whose cancel_reason is PRO_REFUND_CANCEL_REASON (a store refund). Every
// other expiry-only event never changes the status or creates a row. Expiry: while granted,
// expires_at is the expiration_at_ms of the latest grant or expiry-only event that does not revoke;
// a revoke leaves expires_at as it was, so a RENEWAL stamped before a recorded EXPIRATION cannot
// move it. A product without a period (requiresExpiry false, the lifetime) takes expiry-only events
// for nothing and its events carry no expiration_at_ms, so its row keeps expires_at NULL. A product
// with a period (requiresExpiry true, the annual) fails closed: an event without expiration_at_ms
// is ignored for status (a grant) and for expiry (any event), so its granted row never has a NULL
// expires_at, which would mean Pro forever; recordPurchaseEvent still records such a grant and warns
// about it. The (user_id, product_id) key keeps the annual and lifetime rows independent. The row
// is written with source 'revenuecat' only when something differs, so a redelivery leaves
// updated_at untouched. Callers hold the (user, product) advisory lock so the reads see every
// committed event.
import type pg from 'pg';

import { PRO_PRODUCT_RULES, PRO_REFUND_CANCEL_REASON } from '../constants/proProducts.js';
import type { ProProductId } from '../constants/proProducts.js';
import { REVENUECAT_EVENTS } from '../constants/revenueCatEvents.js';

const {
  CANCELLATION_TYPE,
  ENTITLEMENT_SOURCE,
  EXPIRY_ONLY_TYPES,
  GRANT_TYPES,
  PROVIDER,
  REVOKE_TYPES,
  SANDBOX_ENVIRONMENT,
  STORES,
} = REVENUECAT_EVENTS;

type Status = 'granted' | 'revoked';

// One product's events from the stores that can change it, each marked with whether it revokes;
// SANDBOX events only when the server accepts them (Task 3.4). $1 user, $2 product, $3 provider,
// $4 stores, $5 revoke types, $6 CANCELLATION, $7 whether a CANCELLATION revokes on this product,
// $8 the refund cancel_reason, $9 acceptSandbox, $10 SANDBOX. A constant, never user input.
const EVENTS_SQL = `SELECT kind, occurred_at, payload,
    (kind = ANY($5::text[])
      OR (kind = $6 AND ($7::boolean OR payload->>'cancel_reason' IS NOT DISTINCT FROM $8::text))) AS is_revoke
  FROM purchase_events
  WHERE provider = $3 AND user_id = $1 AND product_id = $2 AND payload->>'store' = ANY($4::text[])
    AND ($9::boolean OR payload->>'environment' IS DISTINCT FROM $10::text)`;

function eventParams(userId: string, productId: ProProductId, acceptSandbox: boolean): unknown[] {
  return [
    userId,
    productId,
    PROVIDER,
    [...STORES],
    [...REVOKE_TYPES],
    CANCELLATION_TYPE,
    PRO_PRODUCT_RULES[productId].cancellation === 'revoke',
    PRO_REFUND_CANCEL_REASON,
    acceptSandbox,
    SANDBOX_ENVIRONMENT,
  ];
}

// The latest grant or revoke wins. When requiresExpiry, a grant without expiration_at_ms is skipped;
// a revoke never needs one.
async function readStatus(
  client: pg.PoolClient,
  userId: string,
  productId: ProProductId,
  acceptSandbox: boolean,
): Promise<Status | undefined> {
  const { rows } = await client.query<{ status: Status }>(
    `WITH events AS (${EVENTS_SQL})
     SELECT CASE WHEN is_revoke THEN 'revoked' ELSE 'granted' END AS status
     FROM events
     WHERE is_revoke
        OR (kind = ANY($11::text[]) AND NOT ($12::boolean AND payload->>'expiration_at_ms' IS NULL))
     ORDER BY occurred_at DESC, is_revoke DESC
     LIMIT 1`,
    [...eventParams(userId, productId, acceptSandbox), [...GRANT_TYPES], PRO_PRODUCT_RULES[productId].requiresExpiry],
  );
  return rows[0]?.status;
}

// The latest non-revoking grant or expiry-only event's expiration_at_ms, or null when it carries
// none (the lifetime product). When requiresExpiry, events without one are skipped, and the grant
// that made the row granted carries one, so the answer is never null. Only read while granted: the
// latest grant is then later than every revoke, so this event is too.
async function readExpiryMs(
  client: pg.PoolClient,
  userId: string,
  productId: ProProductId,
  acceptSandbox: boolean,
): Promise<number | null> {
  const { requiresExpiry } = PRO_PRODUCT_RULES[productId];
  const expiryKinds = requiresExpiry ? [...GRANT_TYPES, ...EXPIRY_ONLY_TYPES] : [...GRANT_TYPES];
  const { rows } = await client.query<{ expiration_at_ms: number | null }>(
    `WITH events AS (${EVENTS_SQL})
     SELECT (payload->>'expiration_at_ms')::double precision AS expiration_at_ms
     FROM events
     WHERE NOT is_revoke AND kind = ANY($11::text[])
       AND NOT ($12::boolean AND payload->>'expiration_at_ms' IS NULL)
     ORDER BY occurred_at DESC, (payload->>'expiration_at_ms')::double precision DESC NULLS LAST
     LIMIT 1`,
    [...eventParams(userId, productId, acceptSandbox), expiryKinds, requiresExpiry],
  );
  return rows[0]?.expiration_at_ms ?? null;
}

async function recomputeEntitlement(
  client: pg.PoolClient,
  userId: string,
  productId: ProProductId,
  acceptSandbox: boolean,
): Promise<void> {
  const status = await readStatus(client, userId, productId, acceptSandbox);
  if (!status) {
    return;
  }
  const expiryMs = status === 'granted' ? await readExpiryMs(client, userId, productId, acceptSandbox) : null;
  await client.query(
    `INSERT INTO entitlements (user_id, product_id, source, status, expires_at)
     VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, to_timestamp($5::double precision / 1000))
     ON CONFLICT (user_id, product_id) DO UPDATE SET
       source = EXCLUDED.source,
       status = EXCLUDED.status,
       expires_at = CASE WHEN EXCLUDED.status = 'granted' THEN EXCLUDED.expires_at ELSE entitlements.expires_at END
     WHERE entitlements.status IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.status
        OR entitlements.source IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.source
        OR (EXCLUDED.status = 'granted' AND entitlements.expires_at IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.expires_at)`,
    [userId, productId, ENTITLEMENT_SOURCE, status, expiryMs],
  );
}

export { recomputeEntitlement };
```

node-pg parses `double precision` to a JavaScript number, and `to_timestamp(NULL / 1000)` is NULL, so a lifetime row (no expiry on its events) writes NULL. An annual row only reaches the upsert as `granted` through a grant that carries `expiration_at_ms`, so it never writes NULL while granted. A refund `CANCELLATION` is a revoke, so it never supplies an expiry.

`server/src/services/recordPurchaseEvent.ts` (as left by Tasks 3.1 and 3.5):

- Header: after the line Task 3.1 added about normalising `product_id`, add `// A grant without expiration_at_ms on a product that requires one (the annual, PRO_PRODUCT_RULES) is recorded but ignored by recomputeEntitlement (fail closed), and warned about once.`
- Replace `import { isProProductId, normalizeProductId } from '../constants/proProducts.js';` with `import { isProProductId, normalizeProductId, PRO_PRODUCT_RULES } from '../constants/proProducts.js';` and add `import type { ProProductId } from '../constants/proProducts.js';` below it.
- After `type RecordResult = 'duplicate' | 'recorded';` add

  ```ts
  // A grant with no period end on a product that requires one. Granting it would mean Pro forever,
  // so recomputeEntitlement ignores it; it is still recorded (the claim keeps redeliveries
  // idempotent) and answered 200, so RevenueCat does not retry it.
  function isGrantWithoutRequiredExpiry(productId: ProProductId, event: RevenueCatEvent): boolean {
    return (
      PRO_PRODUCT_RULES[productId].requiresExpiry &&
      (REVENUECAT_EVENTS.GRANT_TYPES as readonly string[]).includes(event.type) &&
      typeof event.expiration_at_ms !== 'number'
    );
  }
  ```

- After the block

  ```ts
  if (!isProProductId(productId)) {
    logger.warn({ eventType: type, reason: 'unmapped_product' }, 'revenuecat event for an unmapped product');
    return 'recorded';
  }
  ```

  add

  ```ts

    logger.warn({ productId, type }, 'annual grant without expiration ignored');
  }
  ```

  The warning is logged after the duplicate check, so a redelivery of the same event id logs nothing more. Only the annual requires an expiry, so the message names it.

`server/src/services/readActiveProRows.ts`:

```ts
// The one active-Pro rule (spec "2. Pro", Server): a user's granted entitlement rows for either Pro
// product, from any source, whose expires_at is NULL (lifetime and admin grants) or later than
// `now` (an annual period still running). hasPro, the profile's pro status, and the admin toggle
// all derive from these rows, so the Ask limit, /v1/me, and the admin page cannot disagree. `now`
// is a parameter so expiry is testable without waiting. Takes a pooled client too, so a caller in a
// transaction reads its own writes.
import type pg from 'pg';

import type { Database } from '../clients/database.js';
import { PRO_PRODUCT_ID_LIST } from '../constants/proProducts.js';
import type { ProProductId } from '../constants/proProducts.js';

type Queryable = Database | pg.PoolClient;

interface ActiveProRow {
  expiresAt: Date | null;
  productId: ProProductId;
  source: string;
}

async function readActiveProRows(queryable: Queryable, userId: string, now: Date): Promise<ActiveProRow[]> {
  const { rows } = await queryable.query<{ expires_at: Date | null; product_id: ProProductId; source: string }>(
    `SELECT product_id, source, expires_at FROM entitlements
     WHERE user_id = $1 AND product_id = ANY($2::text[]) AND status = 'granted'
       AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > $3)
     ORDER BY product_id`,
    [userId, [...PRO_PRODUCT_ID_LIST], now],
  );
  return rows.map(({ expires_at: expiresAt, product_id: productId, source }) => ({ expiresAt, productId, source }));
}

export { readActiveProRows };
export type { ActiveProRow };
```

`server/src/services/hasPro.ts`:

```ts
// Whether a user has Pro at `now` (spec "2. Pro", Server): any row readActiveProRows returns.
import type { Database } from '../clients/database.js';

import { readActiveProRows } from './readActiveProRows.js';

async function hasPro(database: Database, userId: string, now: Date): Promise<boolean> {
  return (await readActiveProRows(database, userId, now)).length > 0;
}

export { hasPro };
```

**Files:**

- Modify: `server/src/constants/revenueCatEvents.ts` (add `TRANSFER_TYPE`), `server/src/constants/webhooks.ts` (add `MAX_TRANSFER_IDS`)
- Modify: `server/src/schemas/revenueCatSchemas.ts` (a new `transfer` schema after `eventType`)
- Modify: `server/src/routes/revenueCatEventHandler.ts` (as left by Tasks 3.3 to 3.5: the header, the imports, `HANDLED_TYPES`, and `createRevenueCatEventHandler`)
- Modify: `server/src/services/recordPurchaseEvent.ts` (`buildPayload`'s parameter, the advisory lock key, the exports)
- Modify: `server/src/services/recomputeEntitlement.ts` (the `if (!status)` branch, as left by Task 3.6)
- Test: `server/src/__tests__/routes/revenueCatWebhookTransfer.integration.test.ts` (new)

**Interfaces:**

- Produces: `REVENUECAT_EVENTS.TRANSFER_TYPE = 'TRANSFER'`, handled from now on; `WEBHOOKS.MAX_TRANSFER_IDS = 20`; `revenueCatSchemas.transfer`, `{ event: { event_timestamp_ms; id; transferred_from: string[]; transferred_to: string[]; type: 'TRANSFER' } }` with the event otherwise loose, each list 1 to 20 ids of at most `MAX_EVENT_ID_LENGTH` characters, and no `app_user_id`, `product_id`, or `store` required (RevenueCat's `TRANSFER` carries no product). A `TRANSFER` that fails it is 400 `INPUT_INVALID_BODY` and records nothing.
- Produces: `transferPurchaseEvents(options: { acceptSandbox: boolean; database: Database; event: TransferEvent; logger: Logger }): Promise<'duplicate' | 'recorded'>`. In one transaction with the statement and lock timeouts: the new user is the first `transferred_to` id that names a user; the old users are the `transferred_from` ids that name users, other than the new one. Every one of those user rows is read `FOR KEY SHARE`, and the `(user, Pro product)` advisory locks `recordPurchaseEvent` takes are taken for all of them in sorted order, so no other event for these users interleaves and two transfers cannot deadlock. The claim insert (`kind` `TRANSFER`, `product_id` NULL, `user_id` the new user or NULL) makes a redelivery `duplicate`. Then `UPDATE purchase_events SET user_id = <new user>` for every RevenueCat event of the old users, and `recomputeEntitlement` for both Pro products and every one of those users. A `SANDBOX` transfer on a server that does not accept sandbox is recorded and moves nothing, with the Task 3.4 warning. A transfer to no known user is recorded and moves nothing.
- Changes: `recomputeEntitlement` revokes a `granted` `revenuecat` row that no event decides any more (its events moved away), keeping its `expires_at`; an `admin` row, a test row, or no row is left as it is. `recordPurchaseEvent.ts` also exports `buildPayload(event: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>)`, `entitlementLockKey(userId, productId)`, and `UUID_PATTERN`, which the transfer reuses.
- Out of reach: a deleted account's purchase events have `user_id` NULL (account deletion, Task 3.13), so a `TRANSFER` from a deleted account's id finds nothing to move. See the open questions.
- The app half (Restore resolves true only when `pro.isPro` is true afterwards, otherwise "No purchases to restore on this account.") is Task 4.5's.

```ts
// TRANSFER moves Pro: when a restore on another account takes purchases over, RevenueCat sends a
// TRANSFER naming the old app user ids (transferred_from) and the new ones (transferred_to), with no
// product or app_user_id. The server records it once, reassigns every RevenueCat purchase event of
// the old users to the first transferred_to id that names a user, and recomputes both Pro products
// for all of them: a lifetime bought on user A, then a TRANSFER from A to B, leaves B with Pro and A
// without. The stored payload keeps neither list of ids. A redelivery moves nothing more, a transfer
// to no known user moves nothing, a SANDBOX transfer moves nothing on a server that does not
// accept sandbox, and a TRANSFER without both id lists is refused with 400 and records nothing.
import { randomBytes, randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';

import request from 'supertest';
import { afterAll, beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, inject, it } from 'vitest';

import { hasPro } from '../../services/hasPro.js';
import { createMigratedDatabase } from '../integration/createMigratedDatabase.js';
import { createWebhookTestApp } from '../integration/createWebhookTestApp.js';
import { SKIP_DATABASE_TESTS } from '../integration/skipDatabaseTests.js';

const ROUTE = '/v1/webhooks/revenuecat';
const HTTP_OK = 200;
const HTTP_BAD_REQUEST = 400;
const SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000;
const DISTINCTIVE_BYTES = 12;
const T0 = 1_790_000_000_000;
const HOUR_MS = 3_600_000;
const YEAR_MS = 31_536_000_000;
const ANNUAL = 'syntactical.pro.annual';
const LIFETIME = 'syntactical.pro.lifetime';
// After every event below and long before the annual period ends.
const NOW = new Date(T0 + 3 * HOUR_MS);

let database: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof createMigratedDatabase>>;

type TestApp = ReturnType<typeof createWebhookTestApp>;

interface EntitlementRow {
  expires_at: Date | null;
  product_id: string;
  status: string;
}

async function insertUser(): Promise<string> {
  const { rows } = await database.pool.query<{ id: string }>('INSERT INTO users (email) VALUES ($1) RETURNING id', [
    `learner-${randomUUID()}@example.com`,
  ]);
  return rows[0].id;
}

function post(testApp: TestApp, event: Record<string, unknown>) {
  return request(testApp.app)
    .post(ROUTE)
    .set('Authorization', testApp.revenueCatAuth)
    .set('Content-Type', 'application/json')
    .send(JSON.stringify({ event }));
}

// A purchase of `productId` by `userId` at T0; the annual carries a one-year period.
function purchase(userId: string, productId: string): Record<string, unknown> {
  const isAnnual = productId === ANNUAL;
  return {
    app_user_id: userId,
    environment: 'SANDBOX',
    event_timestamp_ms: T0,
    ...(isAnnual ? { expiration_at_ms: T0 + YEAR_MS } : {}),
    id: randomUUID(),
    product_id: productId,
    store: 'APP_STORE',
    transaction_id: randomBytes(DISTINCTIVE_BYTES).toString('hex'),
    type: isAnnual ? 'INITIAL_PURCHASE' : 'NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE',
  };
}

function transfer(fromIds: unknown, toIds: unknown): Record<string, unknown> {
  return {
    environment: 'SANDBOX',
    event_timestamp_ms: T0 + HOUR_MS,
    id: randomUUID(),
    store: 'APP_STORE',
    transferred_from: fromIds,
    transferred_to: toIds,
    type: 'TRANSFER',
  };
}

async function rowsOf(userId: string): Promise<EntitlementRow[]> {
  const { rows } = await database.pool.query<EntitlementRow>(
    'SELECT product_id, status, expires_at FROM entitlements WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY product_id',
    [userId],
  );
  return rows;
}

async function countPurchaseEvents(): Promise<number> {
  const { rows } = await database.pool.query<{ count: string }>('SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM purchase_events');
  return Number(rows[0].count);
}

describe.skipIf(SKIP_DATABASE_TESTS)('POST /v1/webhooks/revenuecat TRANSFER', () => {

  });

  it('a lifetime bought on user A, then a TRANSFER from A to B, leaves B Pro and A not', async () => {
    const testApp = createWebhookTestApp({ pool: database.pool });
    const userA = await insertUser();
    const userB = await insertUser();
    await post(testApp, purchase(userA, LIFETIME));

    const response = await post(testApp, transfer([userA], [userB]));

    expect(response.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);
    expect(response.body).toEqual({ data: { status: 'recorded' } });
    expect(await hasPro(database.pool, userB, NOW)).toBe(true);
    expect(await hasPro(database.pool, userA, NOW)).toBe(false);
    expect(await rowsOf(userB)).toEqual([{ expires_at: null, product_id: LIFETIME, status: 'granted' }]);
    expect(await rowsOf(userA)).toEqual([{ expires_at: null, product_id: LIFETIME, status: 'revoked' }]);
    const { rows } = await database.pool.query<{ payload: Record<string, unknown>; product_id: string | null }>(
      "SELECT payload, product_id FROM purchase_events WHERE kind = 'TRANSFER'",
    );
    expect(rows).toEqual([
      {
        payload: { environment: 'SANDBOX', event_timestamp_ms: T0 + HOUR_MS, store: 'APP_STORE', type: 'TRANSFER' },
        product_id: null,
      },
    ]);
  });

  it('moves an annual grant with its expiry', async () => {
    const testApp = createWebhookTestApp({ pool: database.pool });

    const userB = await insertUser();

    await post(testApp, transfer([userA], [userB]));

    expect(await rowsOf(userB)).toEqual([

  });

      expect(response.body.error.code).toBe('INPUT_INVALID_BODY');

    expect(await countPurchaseEvents()).toBe(0);

});
```

`server/src/services/transferPurchaseEvents.ts`:

```ts
// Records one RevenueCat TRANSFER and moves Pro with it. RevenueCat sends a TRANSFER when a restore
// on another app user id (a second account, or the same person signed up again) takes purchases
// over. In one transaction with the statement and lock timeouts: the new user is the first
// transferred_to id that names a user; the old users are the transferred_from ids that name users.
// Their rows are read FOR KEY SHARE and every (user, Pro product) advisory lock recordPurchaseEvent
// uses is taken in one sorted order, so no other event for these users interleaves. The claim
// insert (kind TRANSFER, product_id NULL, user_id the new user) keeps a redelivery idempotent.
// Then every RevenueCat purchase event of the old users is reassigned to the new user, and both Pro
// products are recomputed for all of them: the new user gains what the old users had, and an old
// user whose events all moved loses it. A SANDBOX transfer moves nothing unless acceptSandbox. A
// deleted user's events have user_id NULL and cannot be moved. The stored payload is the scalar
// allowlist, so neither list of ids is stored, and no id is logged.
import type pg from 'pg';
import type { Logger } from 'pino';

import type { Database } from '../clients/database.js';
import { withTransaction } from '../clients/withTransaction.js';
import { PRO_PRODUCT_ID_LIST } from '../constants/proProducts.js';
import { REVENUECAT_EVENTS } from '../constants/revenueCatEvents.js';

import { recomputeEntitlement } from './recomputeEntitlement.js';
import { buildPayload, entitlementLockKey, UUID_PATTERN } from './recordPurchaseEvent.js';

interface TransferEvent {
  [key: string]: unknown;
  event_timestamp_ms: number;
  id: string;
  transferred_from: string[];
  transferred_to: string[];
  type: string;
}

interface TransferPurchaseEventsOptions {
  acceptSandbox: boolean;
  database: Database;
  event: TransferEvent;
  logger: Logger;
}

type TransferResult = 'duplicate' | 'recorded';

// The ids among `ids` that name an existing user, lowercased; each user row read FOR KEY SHARE.
async function lockExistingUsers(client: pg.PoolClient, ids: readonly string[]): Promise<Set<string>> {
  const candidates = [...new Set(ids.filter((id) => UUID_PATTERN.test(id)).map((id) => id.toLowerCase()))];
  if (candidates.length === 0) {
    return new Set();
  }
  const { rows } = await client.query<{ id: string }>(
    'SELECT id FROM users WHERE id = ANY($1::uuid[]) ORDER BY id FOR KEY SHARE',
    [candidates],
  );
  return new Set(rows.map(({ id }) => id));
}

async function transferPurchaseEvents(options: TransferPurchaseEventsOptions): Promise<TransferResult> {
  const { acceptSandbox, database, event, logger } = options;
  const { event_timestamp_ms: eventTimestampMs, id, transferred_from: fromIds, transferred_to: toIds, type } = event;

  return withTransaction<TransferResult>(
    database,
    async (client) => {
      const knownToIds = await lockExistingUsers(client, toIds);
      const newUserId = toIds.map((toId) => toId.toLowerCase()).find((toId) => knownToIds.has(toId)) ?? null;
      const oldUserIds = [...(await lockExistingUsers(client, fromIds))].filter((fromId) => fromId !== newUserId);
      const affectedUserIds = newUserId ? [newUserId, ...oldUserIds].sort() : [];
      for (const userId of affectedUserIds) {
        for (const productId of PRO_PRODUCT_ID_LIST) {
          await client.query('SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended($1, 0))', [
            entitlementLockKey(userId, productId),
          ]);
        }
      }
      const { rowCount } = await client.query(
        `INSERT INTO purchase_events (provider, provider_event_id, kind, product_id, user_id, occurred_at, payload)
         VALUES ($1, $2, $3, NULL, $4, to_timestamp($5::double precision / 1000), $6::jsonb)
         ON CONFLICT (provider, provider_event_id) DO NOTHING`,
        [REVENUECAT_EVENTS.PROVIDER, id, type, newUserId, eventTimestampMs, JSON.stringify(buildPayload(event))],
      );
      if (rowCount === 0) {
        return 'duplicate';
      }
      if (event.environment === REVENUECAT_EVENTS.SANDBOX_ENVIRONMENT && !acceptSandbox) {
        logger.warn({ eventType: type, reason: 'sandbox' }, 'revenuecat sandbox event not applied');
        return 'recorded';
      }
      if (!newUserId || oldUserIds.length === 0) {
        return 'recorded';
      }
      await client.query('UPDATE purchase_events SET user_id = $1 WHERE provider = $2 AND user_id = ANY($3::uuid[])', [
        newUserId,
        REVENUECAT_EVENTS.PROVIDER,
        oldUserIds,
      ]);
      for (const userId of affectedUserIds) {
        for (const productId of PRO_PRODUCT_ID_LIST) {
          await recomputeEntitlement(client, userId, productId, acceptSandbox);
        }
      }
      return 'recorded';
    },
    { hasTimeouts: true },
  );
}

export { transferPurchaseEvents };
export type { TransferEvent };
```

  ```ts
  function createRevenueCatEventHandler(options: EventHandlerOptions): RequestHandler {
    const { acceptSandbox, database, logger } = options;
    return async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
      const typed = revenueCatSchemas.eventType.safeParse(req.body);
      if (!typed.success) {
        sendInvalidBody(res);
        return;
      }
      const { type } = typed.data.event;
      if (!HANDLED_TYPES.has(type)) {
        res.status(OK).json({ data: { status: 'ignored' } });
        return;
      }
      const log = requestLog(res, logger);
      if (type === TRANSFER_TYPE) {
        const transfer = revenueCatSchemas.transfer.safeParse(req.body);
        if (!transfer.success) {
          sendInvalidBody(res);
          return;
        }
        const status = await transferPurchaseEvents({
          acceptSandbox,
          database,
          event: transfer.data.event,
          logger: log,
        });
        res.status(OK).json({ data: { status } });
        return;
      }
      const { data, success } = revenueCatSchemas.webhook.safeParse(req.body);
      if (!success) {
        sendInvalidBody(res);
        return;
      }
      const status = await recordPurchaseEvent({ acceptSandbox, database, event: data.event, logger: log });
      res.status(OK).json({ data: { status } });
    };
  }
  ```

```ts
// beside the routes an admin grant must reach: the /v1 sync routes (GET /v1/me) and the RevenueCat
```

```ts
// Requests and database reads shared by the /v1/admin/access integration tests: sign in a user
// (an admin when the test sets users.is_admin directly, the only way the flag is ever set), call
// the admin routes by bearer token or by cookie, and read or insert a user's entitlement rows,
// expiry included.
import type pg from 'pg';
import request from 'supertest';

import { insertSession } from './insertSession.js';

export const ADMIN_ACCESS_ROUTE = '/v1/admin/access';
const COOKIE_NAME = 'syntactical_session';

export interface Caller {
  sessionToken: string;
  transport: 'bearer' | 'cookie';
  userId: string;
}

export interface EntitlementRow {
  expires_at: Date | null;
  product_id: string;
  source: string;
  status: string;
  updated_at: Date;
}

type App = Parameters<typeof request>[0];

export async function signInUser(pool: pg.Pool, now: Date, isAdmin: boolean): Promise<Caller> {
  const { sessionToken, userId } = await insertSession(pool, { createdAt: now });
  if (isAdmin) {
    await pool.query('UPDATE users SET is_admin = true WHERE id = $1', [userId]);
  }
  return { sessionToken, transport: 'bearer', userId };
}

export function asCookie(caller: Caller): Caller {
  return { ...caller, transport: 'cookie' };
}

export function authorize(pending: request.Test, caller: Caller, withCsrfHeader = true): request.Test {
  if (caller.transport === 'bearer') {
    return pending.set('Authorization', `Bearer ${caller.sessionToken}`);
  }
  const withCookie = pending.set('Cookie', `${COOKIE_NAME}=${caller.sessionToken}`);
  return withCsrfHeader ? withCookie.set('X-Requested-With', 'XMLHttpRequest') : withCookie;
}

export function getAccess(app: App, caller: Caller): Promise<request.Response> {
  return authorize(request(app).get(ADMIN_ACCESS_ROUTE), caller).then((response) => response);
}

export function putAccess(app: App, caller: Caller, body: unknown): Promise<request.Response> {
  return authorize(request(app).put(ADMIN_ACCESS_ROUTE), caller)
    .send(body as object)
    .then((response) => response);
}

export async function readEntitlementRows(pool: pg.Pool, userId: string): Promise<EntitlementRow[]> {
  const { rows } = await pool.query<EntitlementRow>(
    `SELECT product_id, source, status, expires_at, updated_at FROM entitlements
     WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY product_id`,
    [userId],
  );
  return rows;
}

export async function insertEntitlement(
  pool: pg.Pool,
  row: { expiresAt?: Date | null; productId: string; source: string; status: 'granted' | 'revoked'; userId: string },
): Promise<void> {
  await pool.query(
    'INSERT INTO entitlements (user_id, product_id, source, status, expires_at) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5)',
    [row.userId, row.productId, row.source, row.status, row.expiresAt ?? null],
  );
}

export async function readIsAdmin(pool: pg.Pool, userId: string): Promise<boolean | undefined> {
  const { rows } = await pool.query<{ is_admin: boolean }>('SELECT is_admin FROM users WHERE id = $1', [userId]);
  return rows[0]?.is_admin;
}
```

```ts
// Admin access as a Pro toggle (spec "2. Pro", Server): GET /v1/admin/access answers one entry in
// today's AdminProductEntry shape, { grantSource, isGranted, productId: 'syntactical.pro.lifetime' }.
// grantSource is 'purchase' when a granted RevenueCat row on either Pro product is active (expires_at
// NULL or later than now), else 'admin' for the admin's own lifetime grant, else null; isGranted is
// true exactly when grantSource is set. PUT /v1/admin/access { isGranted } grants or revokes an
// 'admin'-source lifetime row with no expiry for the session user only and answers the same entry.
// A granted 'revenuecat' row is never overwritten. A request needs a session (401

    const afterRevoke = await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId);
    const hasProAfterRevoke = await hasPro(database.pool, admin.userId, now);
    const regranted = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: true });

    expect(revoked.body).toEqual(entry(null));
    expect(afterRevoke.filter(({ status }) => status === 'granted')).toEqual([]);
    expect(hasProAfterRevoke).toBe(false);
    expect(regranted.body).toEqual(entry('admin'));
    expect(shape(await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId))).toEqual([
      { expires_at: null, product_id: LIFETIME, source: 'admin', status: 'granted' },
    ]);

      userId: admin.userId,

    const turnedOff = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: false });

    for (const response of [turnedOn, turnedOff]) {

      productId: LIFETIME,
      source: 'revenuecat',
      status: 'revoked',
      userId: admin.userId,
    });

    const response = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: true });

    expect(response.body).toEqual(entry('admin'));
    expect(shape(await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId))).toEqual([
      { expires_at: null, product_id: LIFETIME, source: 'admin', status: 'granted' },
    ]);

  it("PUT leaves an active annual row alone, writes only the lifetime row, and answers 'purchase'", async () => {
    const { app, now } = setup();
    const admin = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);
    const annualExpiry = new Date(now.getTime() + DAY_MS);
    await insertEntitlement(database.pool, {
      expiresAt: annualExpiry,
      productId: ANNUAL,
      source: 'revenuecat',
      status: 'granted',
      userId: admin.userId,
    });

    const turnedOn = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: true });
    const turnedOff = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: false });

    for (const response of [turnedOn, turnedOff]) {
      expect(response.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);
      expect(response.body).toEqual(entry('purchase'));
    }
    expect(shape(await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId))).toEqual([
      { expires_at: annualExpiry, product_id: ANNUAL, source: 'revenuecat', status: 'granted' },
      { expires_at: null, product_id: LIFETIME, source: 'admin', status: 'revoked' },
    ]);
  });

  it('PUT refuses a productId field or a missing or non-boolean isGranted with 400 and writes nothing', async () => {
    const { app, now } = setup();
    const admin = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);

    for (const body of [
      { isGranted: true, productId: LIFETIME },
      { isGranted: true, productId: 'syntactical.python.medium' },
      {},
      { isGranted: 'true' },
      { isGranted: null },

      const response = await putAccess(app, admin, body);

      expect(response.body.error.code).toBe('INPUT_INVALID_BODY');

  it("PUT changes only the session user's rows, never another user's", async () => {
    const { app, now } = setup();

    const revoked = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: false });

    expect(granted.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);
    expect(revoked.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);
```

`server/src/__tests__/routes/adminAccessEntitlements.integration.test.ts`, replaced whole:

```ts
// The admin Pro toggle end to end (spec "2. Pro", Server): an admin's self-grant through PUT
// /v1/admin/access makes hasPro true with no expiry, and a revoke makes it false again. Purchases
// win: a RevenueCat lifetime purchase delivered through the webhook takes over an admin-granted row
// (granted, source 'revenuecat'), and a later toggle off leaves the purchase in force. An annual
// purchase is a separate row the toggle never touches, and GET reports it as 'purchase' while it is
// active. Every token is built at run time.
import { randomBytes, randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';

import request from 'supertest';
import { afterAll, beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, inject, it } from 'vitest';

import { hasPro } from '../../services/hasPro.js';
import { getAccess, putAccess, readEntitlementRows, signInUser } from '../integration/adminAccessRequests.js';
import { ADMIN_TEST_PRODUCTS, createAdminTestApp } from '../integration/createAdminTestApp.js';
import { createMigratedDatabase } from '../integration/createMigratedDatabase.js';
import { SKIP_DATABASE_TESTS } from '../integration/skipDatabaseTests.js';

const HTTP_OK = 200;
const SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000;
const WEBHOOK_ROUTE = '/v1/webhooks/revenuecat';
const TRANSACTION_BYTES = 12;
const YEAR_MS = 31_536_000_000;
const { ANNUAL, LIFETIME } = ADMIN_TEST_PRODUCTS;
// The toggle's entry while a purchase is in force (today's AdminProductEntry shape).
const PURCHASED = { data: { grantSource: 'purchase', isGranted: true, productId: LIFETIME } };

let database: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof createMigratedDatabase>>;

type App = ReturnType<typeof createAdminTestApp>['app'];

function setup() {
  const testApp = createAdminTestApp({ pool: database.pool });
  return { ...testApp, now: testApp.clock.now() };
}

function deliverPurchase(app: App, revenueCatAuth: string, userId: string, productId: string, at: Date) {
  const isAnnual = productId === ANNUAL;
  const event = {
    app_user_id: userId,
    environment: 'SANDBOX',
    event_timestamp_ms: at.getTime(),
    ...(isAnnual ? { expiration_at_ms: at.getTime() + YEAR_MS } : {}),
    id: randomUUID(),
    product_id: productId,
    purchased_at_ms: at.getTime(),
    store: 'APP_STORE',
    transaction_id: randomBytes(TRANSACTION_BYTES).toString('hex'),
    type: isAnnual ? 'INITIAL_PURCHASE' : 'NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE',
  };
  return request(app)
    .post(WEBHOOK_ROUTE)
    .set('Authorization', revenueCatAuth)
    .set('Content-Type', 'application/json')
    .send(JSON.stringify({ event }));
}

function shape(rows: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof readEntitlementRows>>) {
  return rows.map(({ product_id, source, status }) => ({ product_id, source, status }));
}

describe.skipIf(SKIP_DATABASE_TESTS)('the admin Pro toggle reaches hasPro and yields to purchases', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    database = await createMigratedDatabase(inject('testDatabaseUrl'));
  }, SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);

  afterAll(async () => {
    await database?.drop();
  });

  beforeEach(async () => {
    await database.reset();
  });

  it('a self-grant gives Pro with no expiry, and a revoke takes it away', async () => {
    const { app, now } = setup();
    const admin = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);

    const before = await hasPro(database.pool, admin.userId, now);
    const granted = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: true });
    const whileGranted = await hasPro(database.pool, admin.userId, now);
    const farFuture = await hasPro(database.pool, admin.userId, new Date(now.getTime() + 100 * YEAR_MS));
    const revoked = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: false });
    const afterRevoke = await hasPro(database.pool, admin.userId, now);

    expect(before).toBe(false);
    expect(granted.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);
    expect(whileGranted).toBe(true);
    expect(farFuture).toBe(true);
    expect(revoked.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);
    expect(afterRevoke).toBe(false);
  });

  it('a RevenueCat lifetime purchase takes over an admin-granted row, and a later toggle off leaves it in force', async () => {
    const { app, now, revenueCatAuth } = setup();
    const admin = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);

    const granted = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: true });
    const delivered = await deliverPurchase(app, revenueCatAuth, admin.userId, LIFETIME, now);
    const rowsAfterPurchase = await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId);
    const listedAfterPurchase = await getAccess(app, admin);
    const toggledOff = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: false });
    const rowsAfterToggle = await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId);

    expect(granted.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);
    expect(delivered.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);
    expect(shape(rowsAfterPurchase)).toEqual([{ product_id: LIFETIME, source: 'revenuecat', status: 'granted' }]);
    expect(listedAfterPurchase.body).toEqual(PURCHASED);
    expect(toggledOff.body).toEqual(PURCHASED);
    expect(rowsAfterToggle).toEqual(rowsAfterPurchase);
    expect(await hasPro(database.pool, admin.userId, now)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('a toggle off with an active annual purchase leaves the annual row and Pro in force', async () => {
    const { app, now, revenueCatAuth } = setup();
    const admin = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);

    await deliverPurchase(app, revenueCatAuth, admin.userId, ANNUAL, now);
    await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: true });
    const toggledOff = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: false });
    const listed = await getAccess(app, admin);

    expect(shape(await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId))).toEqual([
      { product_id: ANNUAL, source: 'revenuecat', status: 'granted' },
      { product_id: LIFETIME, source: 'admin', status: 'revoked' },
    ]);
    expect(await hasPro(database.pool, admin.userId, now)).toBe(true);
    for (const response of [toggledOff, listed]) {
      expect(response.body).toEqual(PURCHASED);
    }
  });
});
```

`server/src/__tests__/routes/adminAccessGuards.integration.test.ts`, replaced whole:

```ts
// Guards on PUT /v1/admin/access (spec "2. Pro", Server): a cookie request needs the CSRF header;
// the body is JSON only; malformed, oversized, mistyped, and injection-shaped bodies are refused
// and write nothing; a productId, userId, or isAdmin field is refused and never reaches another
// user or the admin flag; the admin flag is read on every request; and the PUT is rate limited per
// user at 60 an hour, the 61st answering 429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED and changing nothing. Every token
// is built at run time.
import request from 'supertest';
import { afterAll, beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, inject, it } from 'vitest';

import {
  ADMIN_ACCESS_ROUTE,
  asCookie,
  authorize,
  getAccess,
  insertEntitlement,
  putAccess,
  readEntitlementRows,
  readIsAdmin,
  signInUser,
} from '../integration/adminAccessRequests.js';
import { ADMIN_TEST_PRODUCTS, createAdminTestApp } from '../integration/createAdminTestApp.js';
import { createMigratedDatabase } from '../integration/createMigratedDatabase.js';
import { SKIP_DATABASE_TESTS } from '../integration/skipDatabaseTests.js';

const HTTP_OK = 200;
const HTTP_BAD_REQUEST = 400;
const HTTP_FORBIDDEN = 403;
const HTTP_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE = 413;
const HTTP_UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE = 415;
const HTTP_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS = 429;
const SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000;
const RATE_LIMIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000;
const HOUR_MS = 3_600_000;
// The chosen limit, written out so the test does not borrow the code's constant.
const PUTS_PER_HOUR = 60;
const OVERSIZED_BYTES = 20_000;
const { LIFETIME } = ADMIN_TEST_PRODUCTS;

let database: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof createMigratedDatabase>>;

function setup() {
  const testApp = createAdminTestApp({ pool: database.pool });
  return { ...testApp, now: testApp.clock.now() };
}

function grantedProductIds(rows: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof readEntitlementRows>>): string[] {
  return rows.filter(({ status }) => status === 'granted').map(({ product_id }) => product_id);
}

describe.skipIf(SKIP_DATABASE_TESTS)('PUT /v1/admin/access guards', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    database = await createMigratedDatabase(inject('testDatabaseUrl'));
  }, SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);

  afterAll(async () => {
    await database?.drop();
  });

  beforeEach(async () => {
    await database.reset();
  });

  it('refuses a cookie PUT without X-Requested-With with 403 and accepts it with the header', async () => {
    const { app, now } = setup();
    const admin = asCookie(await signInUser(database.pool, now, true));

    const withoutHeader = await authorize(request(app).put(ADMIN_ACCESS_ROUTE), admin, false).send({
      isGranted: true,
    });
    const rowsAfterRefusal = await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId);
    const withHeader = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: true });

    expect(withoutHeader.status).toBe(HTTP_FORBIDDEN);
    expect(withoutHeader.body.error.code).toBe('CSRF_HEADER_MISSING');
    expect(rowsAfterRefusal).toEqual([]);
    expect(withHeader.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);
    expect(grantedProductIds(await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId))).toEqual([LIFETIME]);
  });

  it('accepts JSON only: a form or text body is refused with 415 and writes nothing', async () => {
    const { app, now } = setup();
    const admin = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);

    const form = await authorize(request(app).put(ADMIN_ACCESS_ROUTE), admin).type('form').send('isGranted=true');
    const text = await authorize(request(app).put(ADMIN_ACCESS_ROUTE), admin)
      .set('Content-Type', 'text/plain')
      .send(JSON.stringify({ isGranted: true }));
    const rowsAfterRefusals = await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId);
    const json = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: true });

    for (const response of [form, text]) {
      expect(response.status).toBe(HTTP_UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE);
      expect(response.body.error.code).toBe('INPUT_UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE');
    }
    expect(rowsAfterRefusals).toEqual([]);
    expect(json.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);
  });

  it('refuses malformed JSON, an oversized body, and every mistyped or injection-shaped body, writing nothing', async () => {
    const { app, now } = setup();
    const admin = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);

    const malformed = await authorize(request(app).put(ADMIN_ACCESS_ROUTE), admin)
      .set('Content-Type', 'application/json')
      .send('{"isGranted": tru');
    const oversized = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: true, padding: 'x'.repeat(OVERSIZED_BYTES) });
    expect(malformed.status).toBe(HTTP_BAD_REQUEST);
    expect(malformed.body.error.code).toBe('INPUT_MALFORMED_JSON');
    expect(oversized.status).toBe(HTTP_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE);

    const invalidBodies: unknown[] = [
      {},
      { isGranted: 'true' },
      { isGranted: 1 },
      { isGranted: null },
      { isGranted: [true] },
      { isGranted: { $ne: false } },
      { isGranted: true, productId: LIFETIME },
      { isGranted: true, productId: "'; UPDATE users SET is_admin = true; --" },
      { isGranted: true, product: LIFETIME },
      [{ isGranted: true }],
    ];
    for (const body of invalidBodies) {
      const response = await putAccess(app, admin, body);
      expect({ body, status: response.status }).toEqual({ body, status: HTTP_BAD_REQUEST });
      expect(response.body.error.code).toBe('INPUT_INVALID_BODY');
    }
    expect(await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId)).toEqual([]);
    const control = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: true });

    expect(control.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);
    expect(grantedProductIds(await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId))).toEqual([LIFETIME]);
    const { rows } = await database.pool.query<{ count: number }>(
      'SELECT count(*)::int AS count FROM users WHERE is_admin',
    );
    expect(rows).toEqual([{ count: 1 }]);
  });

  it('a userId field never grants to or revokes from another user: refused with 400', async () => {
    const { app, now } = setup();
    const admin = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);
    const target = await signInUser(database.pool, now, false);
    await insertEntitlement(database.pool, {
      productId: LIFETIME,
      source: 'admin',
      status: 'granted',
      userId: target.userId,
    });
    const targetBefore = await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, target.userId);

    const grantForOther = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: true, userId: target.userId });
    const revokeForOther = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: false, userId: target.userId });
    const snakeCase = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: false, user_id: target.userId });

    for (const response of [grantForOther, revokeForOther, snakeCase]) {
      expect(response.status).toBe(HTTP_BAD_REQUEST);
    }
    expect(await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, target.userId)).toEqual(targetBefore);
    expect(await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId)).toEqual([]);
    expect(await readIsAdmin(database.pool, target.userId)).toBe(false);
  });

  it('an isAdmin field never sets the flag, for a non-admin or for another user', async () => {
    const { app, now } = setup();
    const admin = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);
    const learner = await signInUser(database.pool, now, false);

    const fromLearner = await putAccess(app, learner, { isAdmin: true, isGranted: true });
    const fromAdmin = await putAccess(app, admin, { isAdmin: true, isGranted: true, userId: learner.userId });

    expect(fromLearner.status).toBe(HTTP_FORBIDDEN);
    expect(fromLearner.body.error.code).toBe('ADMIN_REQUIRED');
    expect(fromAdmin.status).toBe(HTTP_BAD_REQUEST);
    expect(await readIsAdmin(database.pool, learner.userId)).toBe(false);
    expect(await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, learner.userId)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('reads the admin flag on every request: once cleared, the same session gets 403 and changes nothing', async () => {
    const { app, now } = setup();
    const admin = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);

    const whileAdmin = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: true });
    await database.pool.query('UPDATE users SET is_admin = false WHERE id = $1', [admin.userId]);
    const listed = await getAccess(app, admin);
    const revoke = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: false });

    expect(whileAdmin.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);
    for (const response of [listed, revoke]) {
      expect(response.status).toBe(HTTP_FORBIDDEN);
      expect(response.body.error.code).toBe('ADMIN_REQUIRED');
    }
    expect(grantedProductIds(await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId))).toEqual([LIFETIME]);
  });

  it(
    'allows 60 PUTs an hour per user, refuses the 61st with 429 changing nothing, and limits each user separately',
    async () => {
      const { app, clock, now } = setup();
      const admin = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);
      const otherAdmin = await signInUser(database.pool, now, true);

      for (let index = 0; index < PUTS_PER_HOUR; index += 1) {
        const response = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: index % 2 === 0 });
        expect({ index, status: response.status }).toEqual({ index, status: HTTP_OK });
      }
      // The 60th PUT (index 59) revoked; the 61st would grant.
      const pastLimit = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: true });
      const otherUser = await putAccess(app, otherAdmin, { isGranted: true });

      expect(pastLimit.status).toBe(HTTP_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS);
      expect(pastLimit.body.error.code).toBe('RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED');
      expect(grantedProductIds(await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId))).toEqual([]);
      expect(otherUser.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);

      clock.advance(HOUR_MS);
      const nextWindow = await putAccess(app, admin, { isGranted: true });

      expect(nextWindow.status).toBe(HTTP_OK);
      expect(grantedProductIds(await readEntitlementRows(database.pool, admin.userId))).toEqual([LIFETIME]);
    },
    RATE_LIMIT_TIMEOUT_MS,
  );
});
```

```ts
// The admin's Pro toggle state, in the AdminProductEntry shape the app parses, always for the
// lifetime product, from the active Pro rows hasPro reads (readActiveProRows): 'purchase' when any
// active row's source is not 'admin' (a store purchase of either product, an annual included, or a
// test grant); else 'admin' when the admin's own lifetime grant is in force; else not granted. So
// the entry is granted exactly when hasPro is true. Takes a pooled client too, so setAdminAccess
// can answer from inside its transaction.
import type pg from 'pg';

import type { Database } from '../clients/database.js';
import { PRO_PRODUCT_IDS } from '../constants/proProducts.js';
import type { AdminProductEntry } from '../types/AdminProductEntry.js';

import { readActiveProRows } from './readActiveProRows.js';
import type { ActiveProRow } from './readActiveProRows.js';
import { toAdminProductEntry } from './toAdminProductEntry.js';

const ADMIN_SOURCE = 'admin';

type Queryable = Database | pg.PoolClient;

// The source the entry reports: any source but 'admin' first (toAdminProductEntry reads it as
// 'purchase'), then the admin's own grant, else none.
function grantedSourceOf(rows: readonly ActiveProRow[]): string | undefined {
  const purchase = rows.find(({ source }) => source !== ADMIN_SOURCE);
  if (purchase) {
    return purchase.source;
  }
  return rows.length > 0 ? ADMIN_SOURCE : undefined;
}

async function listAdminAccess(queryable: Queryable, userId: string, now: Date): Promise<AdminProductEntry> {
  return toAdminProductEntry(
    PRO_PRODUCT_IDS.LIFETIME,
    grantedSourceOf(await readActiveProRows(queryable, userId, now)),
  );
}

export { listAdminAccess };
```

`server/src/services/setAdminAccess.ts`, replaced whole (the lock and the "purchases win" rule are unchanged; the product is fixed, a grant writes no expiry, and the answer is the GET entry read in the same transaction):

```ts
// PUT /v1/admin/access's write: in one transaction, under the user's row lock, grants or revokes
// the session user's 'admin'-source entitlement on the lifetime Pro product, with expires_at NULL.
// A granted 'revenuecat' row is never changed (the purchase stays in force); a revoked one (a
// refunded purchase) may be re-granted as 'admin'. Revoking touches only an 'admin' row. An annual
// row is never written here. The answer is listAdminAccess read inside the transaction, so a PUT
// reports exactly what a GET would, an active annual purchase included. Undefined when the user is
// gone.
//
// Serialization with the RevenueCat webhook: lockUserRow takes FOR UPDATE on the users row, which
// conflicts with the FOR KEY SHARE that recordPurchaseEvent takes on the same row
// (SELECT id FROM users WHERE id = $1 FOR KEY SHARE) before it writes the entitlement. So a PUT
// waits for an in-flight webhook transaction to commit and then reads its result, and the
// webhook waits for the PUT. The upsert's WHERE is defense in depth for the same rule.
//
// After a refund an admin re-grant (source 'admin') is removed by any later RevenueCat revoke
// event for the same product, because recomputeEntitlement rewrites source and status. This
// fails closed and is intended.
import type { Database } from '../clients/database.js';
import { withTransaction } from '../clients/withTransaction.js';
import { PRO_PRODUCT_IDS } from '../constants/proProducts.js';
import type { AdminProductEntry } from '../types/AdminProductEntry.js';

import { listAdminAccess } from './listAdminAccess.js';
import { lockUserRow } from './lockUserRow.js';

const PRODUCT_ID = PRO_PRODUCT_IDS.LIFETIME;

async function setAdminAccess(
  database: Database,
  userId: string,
  isGranted: boolean,
  now: Date,
): Promise<AdminProductEntry | undefined> {
  return withTransaction(
    database,
    async (client) => {
      if (!(await lockUserRow(client, userId))) {
        return undefined;
      }
      const { rows } = await client.query<{ source: string; status: string }>(
        'SELECT source, status FROM entitlements WHERE user_id = $1 AND product_id = $2',
        [userId, PRODUCT_ID],
      );
      const [row] = rows;
      const isPurchaseInForce = row?.status === 'granted' && row.source !== 'admin';
      if (isGranted && !isPurchaseInForce) {
        await client.query(
          `INSERT INTO entitlements (user_id, product_id, source, status, expires_at)
           VALUES ($1, $2, 'admin', 'granted', NULL)
           ON CONFLICT (user_id, product_id) DO UPDATE SET source = 'admin', status = 'granted', expires_at = NULL
           WHERE entitlements.source = 'admin' OR entitlements.status = 'revoked'`,
          [userId, PRODUCT_ID],
        );
      }
      if (!isGranted && row?.source === 'admin' && row.status === 'granted') {
        await client.query(
          "UPDATE entitlements SET status = 'revoked' WHERE user_id = $1 AND product_id = $2 AND source = 'admin'",
          [userId, PRODUCT_ID],
        );
      }
      return listAdminAccess(client, userId, now);
    },
    { hasTimeouts: true },
  );
}

export { setAdminAccess };
```

`server/src/routes/adminAccess.ts`, replaced whole:

```ts
// GET and PUT /v1/admin/access: an admin reads the Pro toggle (the lifetime product, whether they
// have Pro, and whether it comes from a purchase or their own grant) and grants or revokes their own
// 'admin' access to it. Order: session (401), admin flag read fresh (403 ADMIN_REQUIRED), then for
// PUT the per-user rate limit (429) and the strict { isGranted } body (400). Only the session user's
// rows are ever read, and only their lifetime row written. Every response is no-store. Both answer
// { data: AdminProductEntry }, one entry, by the clock in deps.
import { Router } from 'express';

import { ADMIN } from '../constants/admin.js';
import { HTTP } from '../constants/http.js';
import { ERROR_CODES, sendError } from '../errors.js';
import { createRateLimit } from '../middleware/rateLimit.js';
import { keyOfUser } from '../middleware/rateLimitKeys.js';
import { createRequireAdmin } from '../middleware/requireAdmin.js';
import { createRequireSession } from '../middleware/requireSession.js';
import { adminSchemas } from '../schemas/adminSchemas.js';
import { listAdminAccess } from '../services/listAdminAccess.js';
import { setAdminAccess } from '../services/setAdminAccess.js';

import type { ResolvedAdminDeps } from './adminDeps.js';

const {
  STATUS: { BAD_REQUEST, OK, UNAUTHORIZED },
} = HTTP;

function createAdminAccessRouter(deps: ResolvedAdminDeps): Router {
  const { database, now, rateLimitKeySecret } = deps;
  const router = Router();
  const requireSession = createRequireSession({ database, now });
  const requireAdmin = createRequireAdmin(database);
  const perUser = createRateLimit({
    database,
    keyOf: keyOfUser,
    keySecret: rateLimitKeySecret,
    limit: ADMIN.RATE_LIMIT.ACCESS_UPDATE_PER_USER,
    now,
    scope: ADMIN.RATE_LIMIT_SCOPE.ACCESS_UPDATE,
    windowMs: ADMIN.RATE_LIMIT.WINDOW_MS,
  });

  router.use('/admin/access', (_req, res, next) => {
    res.set('Cache-Control', 'private, no-store');
    next();
  });

  router.get('/admin/access', requireSession, requireAdmin, async (_req, res) => {
    const { session } = res.locals as { session: { userId: string } };
    const entry = await listAdminAccess(database, session.userId, now());
    res.status(OK).json({ data: entry });
  });

  router.put('/admin/access', requireSession, requireAdmin, perUser, async (req, res) => {
    const { session } = res.locals as { session: { userId: string } };
    const { data, success } = adminSchemas.updateAccess.safeParse(req.body);
    if (!success) {
      sendError(res, BAD_REQUEST, ERROR_CODES.INPUT.INVALID_BODY, 'Invalid request body');
      return;
    }
    const entry = await setAdminAccess(database, session.userId, data.isGranted, now());
    if (!entry) {
      sendError(res, UNAUTHORIZED, ERROR_CODES.AUTH.SESSION_REQUIRED, 'Sign-in required');
      return;
    }
    res.status(OK).json({ data: entry });
  });

  return router;
}

export { createAdminAccessRouter };
```

  ```ts
  const INACTIVE: ProStatus = { expiresAt: null, isActive: false, product: null };

  // From the rows hasPro reads (readActiveProRows); the lifetime product wins over the annual.
  async function readPro(queryable: Queryable, userId: string, now: Date): Promise<ProStatus> {
    const rows = await readActiveProRows(queryable, userId, now);
    const winner = rows.find(({ productId }) => productId === PRO_PRODUCT_IDS.LIFETIME) ?? rows[0];
    if (!winner) {
      return INACTIVE;
    }
    return {
      expiresAt: winner.expiresAt?.toISOString() ?? null,
      isActive: true,
      product: winner.productId === PRO_PRODUCT_IDS.LIFETIME ? 'lifetime' : 'annual',
    };
  }
  ```

```ts
    pool: database.pool,
  });
}

// null mounts the route with no model provider, as with no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
async function signIn(modelProvider: ModelProvider | null = createFakeModelProvider()) {
  const { app, clock } = createAskApp(modelProvider ?? undefined);
  const { sessionToken, userId } = await insertSession(database.pool, { createdAt: clock.now() });
  return { app, clock, sessionToken, userId };
}

async function grant(
  userId: string,
  productId: string,
  options: { expiresAt?: Date | null; status?: 'granted' | 'revoked' } = {},
): Promise<void> {
  const { expiresAt = null, status = 'granted' } = options;
  await database.pool.query(
    'INSERT INTO entitlements (user_id, product_id, status, source, expires_at) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5)',
    [userId, productId, status, 'test', expiresAt],
  );
}

type Signed = Awaited<ReturnType<typeof signIn>>;

function ask(signed: Signed, body: object) {
  return request(signed.app)
    .post('/v1/ask')
    .set('Authorization', `Bearer ${signed.sessionToken}`)
    .set('Origin', ALLOWED_ORIGIN)
    .send(body);
}

function askEasy(signed: Signed, extra: object = {}) {
  return ask(signed, { bankKey: EASY_BANK, message: MESSAGE, questionId: easyQuestion.id, ...extra });
}

// Asks `count` times, moving the clock a minute after every burst-limit's worth so only the daily
// limit can refuse; each answer must be 200 with the limit and the answers left.
async function useAnswers(signed: Signed, count: number, limit: number, alreadyUsed = 0): Promise<void> {
  for (let index = 0; index < count; index += 1) {
    if (index > 0 && index % ASK.RATE_LIMIT.PER_USER === 0) signed.clock.advance(MINUTE_MS);
    const response = await askEasy(signed);
    expect({ index, status: response.status }).toEqual({ index, status: 200 });
    expect(response.body.data).toMatchObject({ limit, remaining: limit - alreadyUsed - index - 1 });
  }
  signed.clock.advance(MINUTE_MS);
}

async function usage(userId: string): Promise<Array<{ count: number; usage_date: string }>> {
  const { rows } = await database.pool.query<{ count: number; usage_date: string }>(
    "SELECT to_char(usage_date, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS usage_date, count FROM ask_usage WHERE user_id = $1",
    [userId],
  );
  return rows;
}
```

```ts
// The test-only webhook (plan "Seams and fixtures"): startServer mounts POST /v1/test/webhook only
// when the caller passes the testWebhook start option, which is refused outside NODE_ENV=test like
// every other test seam. The route takes the RevenueCat webhook body with no Authorization header
// and runs the same intake, so a fixture purchase grants Pro exactly as a store purchase does, while
// the real webhook still answers 401 without its header. Without the option the route does not
// exist (404), even under NODE_ENV=test. The server boots on the repository's content directory.
import { randomBytes, randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';

import { pino } from 'pino';
import { afterAll, afterEach, beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, inject, it } from 'vitest';

import { startServer } from '../../startServer.js';
import type { RunningServer } from '../../startServer.js';
import { createMigratedDatabase } from '../integration/createMigratedDatabase.js';
import { SKIP_DATABASE_TESTS } from '../integration/skipDatabaseTests.js';

const SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000;
const SECRET_BYTES = 24;
const HTTP_OK = 200;
const HTTP_BAD_REQUEST = 400;
const HTTP_UNAUTHORIZED = 401;
const HTTP_NOT_FOUND = 404;
const TEST_ROUTE = '/v1/test/webhook';
const REAL_ROUTE = '/v1/webhooks/revenuecat';
const LIFETIME = 'syntactical.pro.lifetime';

let database: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof createMigratedDatabase>>;
let running: RunningServer | undefined;
const logger = pino({ level: 'silent' });

function randomSecret(): string {
  return randomBytes(SECRET_BYTES).toString('hex');
}

function buildSource(nodeEnv: 'development' | 'test'): NodeJS.ProcessEnv {
  return {
    ALLOWED_ORIGINS: 'http://localhost:8081',
    DATABASE_URL: database.databaseUrl,
    EMAIL_FROM: 'Syntactical <sign-in@syntactical.dev>',
    NODE_ENV: nodeEnv,
    PORT: '0',
    RATE_LIMIT_KEY_SECRET: randomSecret(),
    RESEND_API_KEY: randomSecret(),
    REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_AUTH: randomSecret(),
  };
}

async function insertUser(): Promise<string> {
  const { rows } = await database.pool.query<{ id: string }>('INSERT INTO users (email) VALUES ($1) RETURNING id', [
    `learner-${randomUUID()}@example.com`,
  ]);
  return rows[0].id;
}

// Shaped like the app's fixture store event (Task 4.13): no environment, so it is applied whatever
// REVENUECAT_ACCEPT_SANDBOX says.
function purchaseEvent(userId: string): Record<string, unknown> {
  return {
    app_user_id: userId,
    event_timestamp_ms: Date.now(),
    id: randomUUID(),
    product_id: LIFETIME,
    store: 'APP_STORE',
    type: 'NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE',
  };
}

function post(path: string, body: unknown): Promise<Response> {
  if (!running) throw new Error('server not started');
  return fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${running.port}${path}`, {
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    method: 'POST',
  });
}

async function countRows(table: 'entitlements' | 'purchase_events'): Promise<number> {
  const { rows } = await database.pool.query<{ count: string }>(`SELECT count(*) AS count FROM ${table}`);
  return Number(rows[0].count);
}

    SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS,

});
```

```ts
// POST /v1/test/webhook (plan "Seams and fixtures"): the RevenueCat webhook without its
// Authorization check, for the fixture purchase client and e2e. It takes the same body, under the
// same 64 KB JSON limit, and runs the same intake (revenueCatEventHandler.ts), so

// for the testWebhook start option, which only e2e/support/runApi.mts passes and which is refused
// outside NODE_ENV=test; any other server answers 404.
import express, { Router } from 'express';
import type { Logger } from 'pino';

import { WEBHOOKS } from '../constants/webhooks.js';

import { createRevenueCatEventHandler, requireJsonBody } from './revenueCatEventHandler.js';
import type { TestWebhookDeps } from './testWebhookDeps.js';

function createTestWebhookRouter(deps: TestWebhookDeps, logger: Logger): Router {
  const { acceptSandbox, database } = deps;
  const router = Router();
  router.post(
    '/webhook',
    requireJsonBody,
    express.json({ limit: WEBHOOKS.BODY_LIMIT }),
    createRevenueCatEventHandler({ acceptSandbox, database, logger }),
  );
  return router;
}

export { createTestWebhookRouter };
```

`server/DEPLOY.md` line 20: replace the row with the two rows

```md
| `REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_AUTH` | At least 32 characters; the exact `Authorization` header value RevenueCat sends to the webhook. Without it (stub mode) the webhook answers 503 and no purchase grants Pro. | yes | `${REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_AUTH}` |
| `REVENUECAT_ACCEPT_SANDBOX` | Exactly `true` or `false`; unset is `false`. Whether a RevenueCat `SANDBOX` event (TestFlight, Play license testers, Web Billing sandbox, all free) grants or revokes Pro. Set `true` on staging only; never on production. | no | `true` (staging) |
```

Insert before `## Post-deploy checks`:

```md
## RevenueCat webhook

RevenueCat posts every purchase event to `https://api.syntactical.dev/v1/webhooks/revenuecat` with the `Authorization` header set to `REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_AUTH`. A wrong or missing header answers 401 before the body is read. The server reads the event type first: a type it does not handle answers 200 `ignored` and is not stored, whatever fields it carries, so RevenueCat never retries it.

Two products change an entitlement: `syntactical.pro.annual` (auto-renewing, one year) and `syntactical.pro.lifetime` (non-consumable). RevenueCat reports a Google Play subscription as `<subscription id>:<base plan id>`, so the annual bought on Play arrives as `syntactical.pro.annual:yearly`; the server strips the base-plan suffix before matching and stores `syntactical.pro.annual`. Any other product id is recorded and changes nothing. For each product the server keeps one `entitlements` row per user:

- `INITIAL_PURCHASE`, `RENEWAL`, `UNCANCELLATION`, and `NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE` grant. On the annual product the row's `expires_at` is the event's `expiration_at_ms`; the lifetime row has none.
- An annual grant without `expiration_at_ms` is recorded and answered 200 but grants nothing (it would otherwise mean Pro forever), and the server logs a warning, `annual grant without expiration ignored`. Look into any such warning in the logs.
- `EXPIRATION` and `REFUND` revoke either product.
- A store refund reaches RevenueCat as a `CANCELLATION` with `cancel_reason` `CUSTOMER_SUPPORT`. It revokes either product at once.
- Any other `CANCELLATION` on the annual product only updates `expires_at` (auto-renew is off and Pro lasts to the period end); on the lifetime product it revokes.
- `SUBSCRIPTION_EXTENDED` (a store-granted extension) moves the annual's `expires_at` to the new period end and never changes the status.
- `TRANSFER` (a restore on another account) moves Pro: every purchase event of the `transferred_from` users is reassigned to the first `transferred_to` id that names a user, and both products are recomputed for all of them, so the new account gains Pro and the old one loses it. A purchase made by an account that was since deleted cannot be moved (its events no longer name a user), and the admin toggle grants only the admin's own account, so the server has no path for those; treat them case by case.
- Any other type (`BILLING_ISSUE`, `PRODUCT_CHANGE`, and the rest) answers 200 `ignored` and is not stored.

Events apply in `event_timestamp_ms` order, not arrival order, and a revoke wins a tie. A user has Pro while either row is granted and its `expires_at` is empty or in the future. The annual and lifetime rows never affect each other.

Sandbox: an event with `environment` `SANDBOX` is always recorded, but changes an entitlement only where `REVENUECAT_ACCEPT_SANDBOX=true` (staging). On production it grants and revokes nothing, now or later, and the server logs `revenuecat sandbox event not applied` with the event type. TestFlight testers and App Review therefore never get production Pro for free.

Accepted gap, billing grace period: when a renewal payment fails, Apple and Google may keep the subscription active for a grace period and RevenueCat sends `BILLING_ISSUE`. The server ignores `BILLING_ISSUE`, so the annual row expires at the period end it already holds, and the subscriber sees the free tier (sponsored cards, 5 asks a day) during the grace period until a `RENEWAL` arrives and grants it again. This is accepted for launch; revisit it if support tickets show it.

The test-only route `POST /v1/test/webhook` takes the same body with no `Authorization` header, for the fixture purchase store and e2e. It exists only when `startServer` is called with the `testWebhook` option, which it refuses outside `NODE_ENV=test`; only the e2e runner (`e2e/support/runApi.mts`) passes it, and the production entrypoint (`server/src/index.ts`) never does. So no environment variable can turn it on in a deployed server.

To check a deploy:

- Production: send a RevenueCat test event from the dashboard and expect 200 `ignored`.
- Staging (with `REVENUECAT_ACCEPT_SANDBOX=true`): a sandbox purchase of either product shows `"pro": { "isActive": true, ... }` on `GET /v1/me` for that account; a sandbox refund of the annual then shows `"isActive": false`.
```

### Open questions (area 3)

1. **Unhandled event types: recorded or not.** The spec says `BILLING_ISSUE` and `PRODUCT_CHANGE` are "recorded and ignored for status"; the brief and today's code answer them 200 `ignored` without storing a row. Assumption: not stored (Tasks 3.3 and 3.5 pin it). Recording them would mean adding them to `HANDLED_TYPES` while `recomputeEntitlement` ignores them.
2. **RevenueCat field details, unverified offline.** The plan assumes RevenueCat reports a store refund as `CANCELLATION` with `cancel_reason` `CUSTOMER_SUPPORT`, that `SUBSCRIPTION_EXTENDED` carries the new `expiration_at_ms`, and that `TRANSFER` carries `transferred_from` and `transferred_to` arrays and no `product_id`. The staging checks in `server/DEPLOY.md` (Task 3.14) and the cutover refund check (Task 4.16) confirm them before launch; if a field differs, Tasks 3.5 and 3.8 change in their schema and SQL only.
3. **`TRANSFER` from a deleted account.** Account deletion sets `purchase_events.user_id` to NULL (Task 3.13), and the payload never stores the app user id, so a `TRANSFER` whose `transferred_from` names a deleted account moves nothing; that person's restore on a new account grants nothing. Fixing it needs a stored RevenueCat customer mapping, which this area does not add. The runbook says so (Task 3.14).

5. **Admin PUT body.** The strict `{ isGranted }` body means an app build that still sends `productId` gets 400 until area 4 ships. The entry shape does not change: GET and PUT answer one `AdminProductEntry` (`{ grantSource, isGranted, productId }`), which `services/admin/parseAccessEntry.ts` already parses; area 4 reads `data` as that one entry instead of `data.products`. ## Area 4: Pro in the app (`feat/pro-app`)

Risk: standard. Depends on: areas 2 and 3 merged (no locked banks, no paywall on the difficulty route; `GET /v1/me` returns `pro: { isActive, expiresAt, product }` and no `entitlements`; `POST /v1/ask` needs only a session and answers `{ answer, limit, proLimit, remaining, tier }`; the 429 `ASK_DAILY_LIMIT_REACHED` answers `{ error: { code, limit, message, proLimit, requestId, tier } }` with `tier: 'free' | 'pro'` (Task 3.11, Ask by tier); `PUT /v1/admin/access` takes `{ isGranted }`, and `GET` and `PUT` both answer `{ data: { grantSource, isGranted, productId: 'syntactical.pro.lifetime' } }` (Task 3.9, admin access); `POST /v1/test/webhook` exists only when the server is started with the `testWebhook: true` start option, which is refused outside `NODE_ENV=test` (Task 3.12, the test-only webhook route)). Branch: `feat/pro-app`. Do not promote the server to production between the area 3 and area 4 merges: until this area lands, the app on `main` still reads `entitlements` and sends the old admin body.

`constants/proProducts.ts`:

```ts
// The two Pro products the stores sell and the plan each one is. A product id outside these is
// not Pro. The ids match PRODUCT_ID_PATTERN in constants/appConfig.ts.
export const PRO_PRODUCT_IDS = {
  ANNUAL: 'syntactical.pro.annual',
  LIFETIME: 'syntactical.pro.lifetime',
} as const;

export type ProPlan = 'annual' | 'lifetime';

export function readProPlan(productId: string): ProPlan | null {
  if (productId === PRO_PRODUCT_IDS.ANNUAL) return 'annual';
  if (productId === PRO_PRODUCT_IDS.LIFETIME) return 'lifetime';
  return null;
}
```

`state/useProStatus.ts`:

```ts
// The signed-in user's Pro status from GET /me's data.pro, keyed by user id so one account's
// status never answers for another. A guest makes no request. The key sits under the 'me' root, so
// useAdminAccess's invalidation of ['me'] refetches it after an admin grant or revoke.
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';

import { apiFetch } from '../clients/apiClient';
import { HTTP_STATUS_OK } from '../constants/appConfig';
import type { ProPlan } from '../constants/proProducts';

import { useSignedInUserId } from './AuthProvider';

export type ProStatus = { expiresAt: string | null; isPro: boolean; product: ProPlan | null };

export type ProStatusState =
  | { status: 'guest' }
  | { status: 'loading' }
  | { retry: () => void; status: 'error' }
  | ({ status: 'ready' } & ProStatus);

function isExpiry(value: unknown): value is string | null {
  return value === null || (typeof value === 'string' && !Number.isNaN(Date.parse(value)));
}

function isPlan(value: unknown): value is ProPlan | null {
  return value === null || value === 'annual' || value === 'lifetime';
}

// The pro object of a GET /me body, or null when it is missing or any field has the wrong shape.
function parseProStatus(body: unknown): ProStatus | null {
  const pro = (body as { data?: { pro?: unknown } } | null)?.data?.pro;
  if (typeof pro !== 'object' || pro === null) return null;
  const { expiresAt, isActive, product } = pro as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (typeof isActive !== 'boolean' || !isExpiry(expiresAt) || !isPlan(product)) return null;
  return { expiresAt, isPro: isActive, product };
}

export async function fetchProStatus(): Promise<ProStatus> {
  const { body, status } = await apiFetch('me');
  const pro = status === HTTP_STATUS_OK ? parseProStatus(body) : null;
  if (pro === null) throw new Error(`profile request failed with ${status}`);
  return pro;
}

export function buildProStatusKey(userId: string | null) {
  return ['me', userId, 'pro'] as const;
}

export function useProStatus(): ProStatusState {
  const userId = useSignedInUserId();
  const { data, isError, refetch } = useQuery({
    enabled: userId !== null,
    queryFn: fetchProStatus,
    queryKey: buildProStatusKey(userId),
  });
  if (userId === null) return { status: 'guest' };
  if (data) return { ...data, status: 'ready' };
  if (isError) return { retry: () => void refetch(), status: 'error' };
  return { status: 'loading' };
}
```

```tsx
  return jest.mocked(trackEvent).mock.calls.filter(([name]) => name === 'paywall_viewed');
}

describe('ProSheet on native', () => {

    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Forever for €43,99' })).toBeTruthy();
    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Not now' })).toBeTruthy();

    expect(props.onClose).not.toHaveBeenCalled();

  it('shows a message as an alert', async () => {

    expect(screen.getByRole('alert')).toHaveTextContent('The purchase did not go through. Try again.');
  });

  it('records paywall_viewed once with its source, and not again when it re-renders', async () => {
    const { rerender } = await render(<ProSheet {...buildProps({ source: 'ask_limit' })} />);
    await rerender(<ProSheet {...buildProps({ isBuying: true, message: 'x', source: 'ask_limit' })} />);
    expect(listPaywallViews()).toEqual([['paywall_viewed', { source: 'ask_limit' }]]);
  });
});
```
