### Task 6.16: consent and SDK initialisation in `SponsorProvider`, and "Privacy settings"

**Files:**

- Create: `clients/adsConsentClient.ts`, `clients/adsConsentClient.web.ts`, `components/sponsor/PrivacySettingsRow.tsx`
- Modify: `state/SponsorProvider.tsx` (whole file, as Tasks 6.3 and 6.10 leave it), `app/settings.tsx` (imports lines 6-14, `LegalLinks` lines 111-127)
- Test: `state/__tests__/SponsorProvider.test.tsx`, `state/__tests__/SponsorProvider.web.test.tsx`, `components/sponsor/__tests__/PrivacySettingsRow.test.tsx` (all new)

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: the SDK's `AdsConsent.requestInfoUpdate(options?)`, `AdsConsent.loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired()`, `AdsConsent.getConsentInfo()` (`canRequestAds`, `privacyOptionsRequirementStatus`), `AdsConsent.showPrivacyOptionsForm()`, `mobileAds().initialize()`; `isAdMobConfigured`, `readConsentDebugDeviceId`; `logWarning`.
- Produces:
  - `gatherConsentAndInitialize({ debugDeviceId }): Promise<{ canRequestAds: boolean; privacyOptionsRequired: boolean }>`: consent info update (with `{ debugGeography: EEA, testDeviceIdentifiers: [id] }` when a debug device is set), the form if required, then `initialize()` whatever the consent outcome or failure (Review Focus 21); never throws. `showAdsPrivacyOptions(): Promise<{ canRequestAds; privacyOptionsRequired } | null>`. The `.web.ts` twin returns `{ canRequestAds: false, privacyOptionsRequired: false }` and `null` without touching the SDK.
  - `useSponsor()` keeps `eligibility` and `directSponsor` and gains `adsStatus: 'pending' | 'ready' | 'unavailable'`, `isReady: boolean` (`adsStatus === 'ready'`), `privacyOptionsRequired: boolean`, `showPrivacyOptions: () => Promise<void>`. Outside the provider: `hidden`, `null`, `unavailable`, false, false, a no-op. The flow runs once per app session, only on native, only when AdMob is configured, and only once the user is eligible (never for a Pro user). `ready` when the SDK initialised and `canRequestAds` is true; `unavailable` otherwise (cards fall back to house content).
  - `PrivacySettingsRow()`: a "Privacy settings" button that calls `showPrivacyOptions`, rendered only when `privacyOptionsRequired`.

// state/__tests__/SponsorProvider.test.tsx
// On native, SponsorProvider asks for ad consent where required and then initialises the Mobile Ads SDK,
// whether consent was given, declined, or the flow failed (Review Focus 21: the app never blocks on
// consent). Ads may load only when the SDK allows requests. Nothing runs for a Pro user, while Pro status
// loads, or in a build without AdMob ids, and the flow runs once.
import { QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { fireEvent, render, screen, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react-native';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { Pressable, Text } from 'react-native';

import { mobileAdsControl, resetMobileAds } from '../../components/sponsor/__tests__/mobileAdsMock';
import { setExpoExtra } from '../../config/expoConstantsMock';
import { createQueryClient } from '../../config/queryClient';
import { settle } from '../../config/settle';
import { SponsorProvider, useSponsor } from '../SponsorProvider';
import type { ProStatusState } from '../useProStatus';

const mockProStatus: { current: ProStatusState } = { current: { status: 'guest' } };

jest.mock('../useProStatus', () => ({ useProStatus: () => mockProStatus.current }));
jest.mock('../AuthProvider', () => ({ useAuth: () => ({ isHydrated: true }), useSignedInUserId: () => null }));

const CONTENT_BASE_URL = 'https://example.test/content/';
const TEST_ADMOB = { androidAppId: 'a', iosAppId: 'i', isTestAds: true, resultsAdUnitId: {}, tracksAdUnitId: {} };
const CONSENT_FLOW = ['requestInfoUpdate', 'loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired', 'getConsentInfo', 'initialize'];

function Probe() {
  const { adsStatus, eligibility, isReady, privacyOptionsRequired, showPrivacyOptions } = useSponsor();
  return (
    <>
      <Text testID="state">{`${eligibility} ${adsStatus} ${String(isReady)} ${String(privacyOptionsRequired)}`}</Text>
      <Pressable role="button" aria-label="privacy" onPress={() => void showPrivacyOptions()} />
    </>
  );
}

// SponsorProvider queries the direct sponsor (Task 6.10), so it needs the query client the root layout gives it.
const queryClient = createQueryClient();

function Providers({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>{children}</QueryClientProvider>;
}

function buildTree() {
  return (
    <SponsorProvider>
      <Probe />
    </SponsorProvider>
  );
}

async function renderProvider() {
  const view = await render(buildTree(), { wrapper: Providers });
  await settle();
  return view;
}

function readState(): string {
  return screen.getByTestId('state').props.children;
}

beforeEach(() => {
  resetMobileAds();
  queryClient.clear();
  mockProStatus.current = { status: 'guest' };
  setExpoExtra({ admob: TEST_ADMOB, contentBaseUrl: CONTENT_BASE_URL });
});

afterAll(() => setExpoExtra({ contentBaseUrl: CONTENT_BASE_URL }));

describe('SponsorProvider consent on native', () => {
  it('asks for consent, then initialises, then allows ads', async () => {
    await renderProvider();
    expect(mobileAdsControl.calls).toEqual(CONSENT_FLOW);
    expect(mobileAdsControl.lastInfoUpdateOptions).toBeUndefined();
    expect(readState()).toBe('eligible ready true false');
  });

  it('initialises and allows non-personalised ads when the form was declined', async () => {
    mobileAdsControl.form = 'resolve';
    mobileAdsControl.canRequestAds = true;
    await renderProvider();
    expect(mobileAdsControl.calls).toContain('initialize');
    expect(readState()).toBe('eligible ready true false');
  });

  it('still initialises when the consent form fails, and never blocks', async () => {
    const warn = jest.spyOn(console, 'warn').mockImplementation(() => undefined);
    mobileAdsControl.form = 'reject';
    await renderProvider();
    expect(mobileAdsControl.calls).toEqual(CONSENT_FLOW);
    expect(readState()).toBe('eligible ready true false');
    warn.mockRestore();
  });

  it('still initialises when the consent info update fails, but loads no ads the SDK does not allow', async () => {
    const warn = jest.spyOn(console, 'warn').mockImplementation(() => undefined);
    mobileAdsControl.infoUpdate = 'reject';
    mobileAdsControl.canRequestAds = false;
    await renderProvider();
    expect(mobileAdsControl.calls).toContain('initialize');
    expect(readState()).toBe('eligible unavailable false false');
    warn.mockRestore();
  });

  it('reports a failed SDK start as unavailable', async () => {
    const warn = jest.spyOn(console, 'warn').mockImplementation(() => undefined);
    mobileAdsControl.initialize = 'reject';
    await renderProvider();
    expect(readState()).toBe('eligible unavailable false false');
    warn.mockRestore();
  });

  it('exposes the privacy options and reopens them on request', async () => {
    mobileAdsControl.privacyOptionsStatus = 'REQUIRED';
    await renderProvider();
    expect(readState()).toBe('eligible ready true true');
    await fireEvent.press(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'privacy' }));
    await settle();
    expect(mobileAdsControl.calls).toContain('showPrivacyOptionsForm');
  });

  it('forces the EEA form on the debug device in a test build', async () => {
    setExpoExtra({ admob: { ...TEST_ADMOB, consentDebugDeviceId: 'DEVICE-1234' }, contentBaseUrl: CONTENT_BASE_URL });
    await renderProvider();
    expect(mobileAdsControl.lastInfoUpdateOptions).toEqual({
      debugGeography: 1,
      testDeviceIdentifiers: ['DEVICE-1234'],
    });
  });

  it('runs nothing for a Pro user', async () => {
    mockProStatus.current = { expiresAt: null, isPro: true, product: 'lifetime', status: 'ready' };
    await renderProvider();
    expect(mobileAdsControl.calls).toEqual([]);
    expect(readState()).toBe('hidden pending false false');
  });

  it('waits for Pro status, then runs the flow once', async () => {
    mockProStatus.current = { status: 'loading' };
    const view = await renderProvider();
    expect(mobileAdsControl.calls).toEqual([]);
    mockProStatus.current = { expiresAt: null, isPro: false, product: null, status: 'ready' };
    view.rerender(buildTree());
    await waitFor(() => expect(mobileAdsControl.calls).toEqual(CONSENT_FLOW));
    view.rerender(buildTree());
    await settle();
    expect(mobileAdsControl.calls).toEqual(CONSENT_FLOW);
  });

  it('runs nothing in a build without AdMob ids', async () => {
    setExpoExtra({ contentBaseUrl: CONTENT_BASE_URL });
    await renderProvider();
    expect(mobileAdsControl.calls).toEqual([]);
    expect(readState()).toBe('eligible unavailable false false');
  });
});

`clients/adsConsentClient.ts`:

```ts
// The one module that talks to Google's consent (UMP) and Mobile Ads SDKs on iOS and Android, so
// SponsorProvider has one seam (the web build uses adsConsentClient.web.ts). It asks for consent where the
// user's region needs it, then initialises the SDK whatever the answer: requests are non-personalised, so a
// declined form still allows limited ads (Review Focus 21). Every failure is logged and swallowed; the result
// says whether ads may be requested and whether Settings must offer the privacy options form.
import mobileAds, {
  AdsConsent,
  AdsConsentDebugGeography,
  AdsConsentPrivacyOptionsRequirementStatus,
} from 'react-native-google-mobile-ads';

import { logWarning } from './logClient';

export type AdsConsentResult = { canRequestAds: boolean; privacyOptionsRequired: boolean };

type ConsentInfo = Awaited<ReturnType<typeof AdsConsent.getConsentInfo>>;

function toResult(info: ConsentInfo | null): AdsConsentResult {
  return {
    canRequestAds: info?.canRequestAds === true,
    privacyOptionsRequired:
      info?.privacyOptionsRequirementStatus === AdsConsentPrivacyOptionsRequirementStatus.REQUIRED,
  };
}

export async function gatherConsentAndInitialize({
  debugDeviceId,
}: {
  debugDeviceId: string | null;
}): Promise<AdsConsentResult> {
  try {
    await AdsConsent.requestInfoUpdate(
      debugDeviceId === null
        ? undefined
        : { debugGeography: AdsConsentDebugGeography.EEA, testDeviceIdentifiers: [debugDeviceId] },
    );
    await AdsConsent.loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired();
  } catch (err) {
    logWarning({ err }, 'ads consent flow failed');
  }
  const info = await AdsConsent.getConsentInfo().catch((err: unknown) => {
    logWarning({ err }, 'ads consent info unavailable');
    return null;
  });
  try {
    await mobileAds().initialize();
  } catch (err) {
    logWarning({ err }, 'ads SDK failed to initialise');
    return { canRequestAds: false, privacyOptionsRequired: false };
  }
  return toResult(info);
}

export async function showAdsPrivacyOptions(): Promise<AdsConsentResult | null> {
  try {
    return toResult(await AdsConsent.showPrivacyOptionsForm());
  } catch (err) {
    logWarning({ err }, 'ads privacy options form failed');
    return null;
  }
}
```

`state/SponsorProvider.tsx` (replace the file as Tasks 6.3 and 6.10 leave it; the direct sponsor query stays as Task 6.10 wrote it):

```tsx
// Decides once for the whole app whether sponsored cards may render, loads the direct sponsor, and prepares
// native ads. Cards render only after auth has hydrated and Pro status is known, and only for a user who is
// not Pro (a guest never is); while Pro status loads or after it fails every card stays hidden, so a Pro user
// never sees a flash (Review Focus 18). SponsoredCard is the only reader of eligibility. While a user may
// see cards it loads the direct sponsor (sponsor.json) once for the whole app. On iOS and Android, once a
// user may see cards in a build with AdMob ids, it runs the consent flow once and initialises the SDK
// whatever the answer (Review Focus 21); ads load only when the SDK allows requests, and otherwise cards fall
// back to house content. A Pro user and the web build never touch the SDK. Outside the provider every card
// is hidden. Mounted inside AuthProvider in app/_layout.tsx.
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { createContext, useCallback, useContext, useEffect, useMemo, useRef, useState, type ReactNode } from 'react';

import { Platform } from 'react-native';

import { gatherConsentAndInitialize, showAdsPrivacyOptions, type AdsConsentResult } from '../clients/adsConsentClient';
import { readExtraString } from '../config/readExtraString';
import { DIRECT_SPONSOR_STALE_MS } from '../constants/sponsor';
import { loadDirectSponsor } from '../services/sponsor/loadDirectSponsor';
import { isAdMobConfigured, readConsentDebugDeviceId } from '../services/sponsor/readAdMobConfig';
import { readLocalToday } from '../services/progress/readLocalToday';
import type { SponsorContent } from '../services/sponsor/types/SponsorContent';

import { useAuth } from './AuthProvider';
import { type ProStatusState, useProStatus } from './useProStatus';

export type SponsorEligibility = 'eligible' | 'hidden';
export type AdsStatus = 'pending' | 'ready' | 'unavailable';

type SponsorContextValue = {
  adsStatus: AdsStatus;
  directSponsor: SponsorContent | null;
  eligibility: SponsorEligibility;
  isReady: boolean;
  privacyOptionsRequired: boolean;
  showPrivacyOptions: () => Promise<void>;
};

const HIDDEN: SponsorContextValue = {
  adsStatus: 'unavailable',
  directSponsor: null,
  eligibility: 'hidden',
  isReady: false,
  privacyOptionsRequired: false,
  showPrivacyOptions: () => Promise.resolve(),
};
const SponsorContext = createContext<SponsorContextValue>(HIDDEN);

export function readSponsorEligibility(proStatus: ProStatusState, isAuthHydrated: boolean): SponsorEligibility {
  if (!isAuthHydrated) return 'hidden';
  if (proStatus.status === 'guest') return 'eligible';
  if (proStatus.status === 'ready' && !proStatus.isPro) return 'eligible';
  return 'hidden';
}

function canUseNativeAds(): boolean {
  return Platform.OS !== 'web' && isAdMobConfigured();
}

export function SponsorProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const proStatus = useProStatus();
  const { isHydrated } = useAuth();
  const eligibility = readSponsorEligibility(proStatus, isHydrated);
  const [adsStatus, setAdsStatus] = useState<AdsStatus>(() => (canUseNativeAds() ? 'pending' : 'unavailable'));
  const [privacyOptionsRequired, setPrivacyOptionsRequired] = useState(false);
  const hasStarted = useRef(false);
  const isMounted = useRef(true);

  useEffect(() => {
    isMounted.current = true;
    return () => {
      isMounted.current = false;
    };
  }, []);

  const applyResult = useCallback((result: AdsConsentResult) => {
    if (!isMounted.current) return;
    setAdsStatus(result.canRequestAds ? 'ready' : 'unavailable');
    setPrivacyOptionsRequired(result.privacyOptionsRequired);
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (eligibility !== 'eligible' || hasStarted.current || !canUseNativeAds()) return;
    hasStarted.current = true;
    void gatherConsentAndInitialize({ debugDeviceId: readConsentDebugDeviceId() }).then(applyResult);
  }, [applyResult, eligibility]);

  const showPrivacyOptions = useCallback(async () => {
    const result = await showAdsPrivacyOptions();
    if (result !== null) applyResult(result);
  }, [applyResult]);

  const contentBaseUrl = readExtraString('contentBaseUrl');
  const { data: directSponsor = null } = useQuery({
    enabled: eligibility === 'eligible',
    queryFn: () => loadDirectSponsor(contentBaseUrl, readLocalToday()),
    queryKey: ['sponsor', contentBaseUrl],
    staleTime: DIRECT_SPONSOR_STALE_MS,
  });

  const value = useMemo<SponsorContextValue>(
    () => ({
      adsStatus,
      directSponsor,
      eligibility,
      isReady: adsStatus === 'ready',
      privacyOptionsRequired,
      showPrivacyOptions,
    }),
    [adsStatus, directSponsor, eligibility, privacyOptionsRequired, showPrivacyOptions],
  );
  return <SponsorContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</SponsorContext.Provider>;
}

export function useSponsor(): SponsorContextValue {
  return useContext(SponsorContext);
}
```

`components/sponsor/useSponsorNativeAd.ts`:

```ts
// The native ad one sponsored card shows, with its lifecycle held here in app code rather than in the SDK
// (decision 16): one NativeAd.createForAdRequest per card mount, the first time the card may request; the
// loaded ad kept until unmount and then destroyed; an ad that arrives after unmount destroyed at once, with
// no state update and so no report (Review Focus 20). A failed request (no fill) is an error the card falls
// back on.
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';

import { NativeAd, type NativeAdRequestOptions } from 'react-native-google-mobile-ads';

export type SponsorNativeAdState = { error: Error | null; nativeAd: NativeAd | null };

const EMPTY: SponsorNativeAdState = { error: null, nativeAd: null };

export function useSponsorNativeAd(
  adUnitId: string,
  options: NativeAdRequestOptions,
  enabled: boolean,
): SponsorNativeAdState {
  const [state, setState] = useState<SponsorNativeAdState>(EMPTY);
  const isMounted = useRef(true);
  const heldAd = useRef<NativeAd | null>(null);
  const hasRequested = useRef(false);
  // The request reads the options of the render that enabled it; a new object later never re-requests.
  const optionsRef = useRef(options);
  optionsRef.current = options;

  useEffect(() => {
    isMounted.current = true;
    return () => {
      isMounted.current = false;
      heldAd.current?.destroy();
      heldAd.current = null;
    };
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!enabled || hasRequested.current) return;
    hasRequested.current = true;
    void NativeAd.createForAdRequest(adUnitId, optionsRef.current).then(
      (ad) => {
        if (!isMounted.current) {
          ad.destroy();
          return;
        }
        heldAd.current = ad;
        setState({ error: null, nativeAd: ad });
      },
      (error: unknown) => {
        if (!isMounted.current) return;
        setState({ error: error instanceof Error ? error : new Error('native ad request failed'), nativeAd: null });
      },
    );
  }, [adUnitId, enabled]);

  return state;
}
```

`components/sponsor/SponsoredCard.tsx` (replace the Task 6.4 file):

```tsx
// The sponsored card on iOS and Android (the web build uses SponsoredCard.web.tsx), and the one place that
// reads eligibility: nothing renders unless SponsorProvider allows cards, so a Pro user never gets even the
// reserved slot. Otherwise the card sits in its fixed-height SponsoredSlot. With an AdMob unit for the
// placement (Google's test unit in a test build), it requests one non-personalised native ad per card mount,
// once consent allows, with the AdChoices icon top right, and renders it in the card frame: each asset a bare
// Text or Image directly inside its NativeAsset, no touchable wrappers and no media view. While consent or
// the ad is pending the slot shows the empty Sponsored frame, so the ad fills in place without moving
// anything. No unit id, ads unavailable, or a load error (no fill) shows the direct sponsor or the house
// card. useSponsorNativeAd owns the ad and destroys it on unmount, so an ad that arrives after the screen
// left reports nothing (Review Focus 20). ad_shown is reported after the ad has rendered; ad_clicked on the
// SDK's click event.
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';

import { Image, Text } from 'react-native';
import {
  NativeAdChoicesPlacement,
  NativeAdEventType,
  NativeAdView,
  NativeAsset,
  NativeAssetType,
  TestIds,
} from 'react-native-google-mobile-ads';

import { readAdMobPlacement } from '../../services/sponsor/readAdMobConfig';
import type { SponsorPlacement } from '../../services/sponsor/types/SponsorPlacement';
import { useSponsor } from '../../state/SponsorProvider';

import { SPONSOR_CLASSES, SponsoredCardFrame } from './SponsoredCardFrame';
import { SponsorContentSlot } from './SponsorContentSlot';
import { SponsoredSlot, SponsoredSlotPlaceholder } from './SponsoredSlot';
import { useSponsorContent, type SponsorContentState } from './useSponsorContent';
import { useSponsorNativeAd } from './useSponsorNativeAd';

export type SponsoredCardProps = { onShown?: () => void; placement: SponsorPlacement };

const FALLBACK_CALL_TO_ACTION = 'Open';
// One options object for every request: non-personalised, AdChoices top right (the frame keeps that corner
// clear).
const AD_REQUEST_OPTIONS = {
  adChoicesPlacement: NativeAdChoicesPlacement.TOP_RIGHT,
  requestNonPersonalizedAdsOnly: true,
};

function resolveAdUnitId(placement: SponsorPlacement): string | null {
  const unit = readAdMobPlacement(placement);
  if (unit === null) return null;
  return 'adUnitId' in unit ? unit.adUnitId : TestIds.NATIVE;
}

function AdMobCard({ adUnitId, sponsor }: { adUnitId: string; sponsor: SponsorContentState }) {
  const { adsStatus } = useSponsor();
  const { error, nativeAd } = useSponsorNativeAd(adUnitId, AD_REQUEST_OPTIONS, adsStatus === 'ready');
  const { onClicked, onShown } = sponsor;

  useEffect(() => {
    if (nativeAd === null) return undefined;
    onShown('admob');
    const subscription = nativeAd.addAdEventListener(NativeAdEventType.CLICKED, () => onClicked('admob'));
    return () => subscription.remove();
  }, [nativeAd, onClicked, onShown]);

  if (adsStatus === 'unavailable' || error !== null) return <SponsorContentSlot sponsor={sponsor} />;
  if (nativeAd === null) return <SponsoredSlotPlaceholder />;

  const { body, callToAction, headline, icon } = nativeAd;
  const actionLabel = callToAction || FALLBACK_CALL_TO_ACTION;
  const iconAsset = icon ? (
    <NativeAsset assetType={NativeAssetType.ICON}>
      <Image aria-hidden source={{ uri: icon.url }} className={SPONSOR_CLASSES.icon} />
    </NativeAsset>
  ) : undefined;
  return (
    <NativeAdView nativeAd={nativeAd}>
      <SponsoredCardFrame headline={headline} icon={iconAsset}>
        <NativeAsset assetType={NativeAssetType.HEADLINE}>
          <Text className={SPONSOR_CLASSES.headline}>{headline}</Text>
        </NativeAsset>
        {body ? (
          <NativeAsset assetType={NativeAssetType.BODY}>
            <Text numberOfLines={1} className={SPONSOR_CLASSES.body}>
              {body}
            </Text>
          </NativeAsset>
        ) : null}
        <NativeAsset assetType={NativeAssetType.CALL_TO_ACTION}>
          <Text
            role="link"
            aria-label={`Sponsored: ${headline}. ${actionLabel}`}
            className={SPONSOR_CLASSES.actionText}
          >
            {actionLabel}
          </Text>
        </NativeAsset>
      </SponsoredCardFrame>
    </NativeAdView>
  );
}

function NativeSponsoredCard({ onShown, placement }: SponsoredCardProps) {
  const sponsor = useSponsorContent(placement, onShown);
  const [adUnitId] = useState(() => resolveAdUnitId(placement));
  if (adUnitId === null) return <SponsorContentSlot sponsor={sponsor} />;
  return <AdMobCard adUnitId={adUnitId} sponsor={sponsor} />;
}

export function SponsoredCard(props: SponsoredCardProps) {
  const { eligibility } = useSponsor();
  if (eligibility === 'hidden') return null;
  return (
    <SponsoredSlot placement={props.placement}>
      <NativeSponsoredCard {...props} />
    </SponsoredSlot>
  );
}
```

(Step 0 recorded the SDK's names. If the icon field, the subscription's `remove()`, or the options type differs, or `NativeAdView` needs the asset `Text` to have no `numberOfLines`, change this file, `useSponsorNativeAd.ts`, and the shared mock together, never the RED tests' behaviour.)

### Open questions (area 6)

1. **EthicalAds fill signal.** Task 6.12 reads the fill from the promise the manual `ethicalads.load()` returns (a list of the placements that filled), with `ETHICAL_ADS_FILL_CEILING_MS` (5000) as a ceiling at which a placement with a child element counts as a fill. Whether the client's `load()` returns that promise, and what it resolves to, is from memory and unverified offline. Check on the deployed site once a publisher id exists (an unapproved or unfilled placement, then an approved one); if `load()` returns nothing, the ceiling decides alone, and the probe can be tightened to `.ea-content` if the client adds other children.
2. **Slot height.** `SPONSOR_SLOT_HEIGHT` (160) is computed from Tailwind's default line heights for the house card's layout. The device and web checks in Task 6.18 confirm that an AdMob ad with a long headline and an EthicalAds text ad fit; if either is taller, raise the constant (the tests pin only that the height is fixed).
3. **Layout checks outside a browser.** The Jest renderers compute no layout, so no Jest test can fire a real `onLayout`. The native tests pin the reserved height through the slot's style before and after a fill (Tasks 6.2 and 6.17); the position check that Retry does not move is a bounding-box comparison in `sponsoredCard.spec.ts` (Task 6.14) and a row in the device checklist (Task 6.18).
4. **Eligibility resolving after the screen renders.** Decision 15 reserves the slot as soon as eligibility is known. If Pro status is still loading when a results screen or the track list renders (a signed-in user on a slow `/v1/me`), the slot appears when it resolves and shifts the content below it once. Rounds end long after launch, so this is expected only on the track list at a cold start.
5. **App ids in a build without AdMob ids.** Decided rule (Task 6.15): the SDK refuses to start without an app id once the library is linked, so `development`, `preview`, and local builds (and the web export) without the variables carry Google's sample app ids and request nothing unless they are test builds, which always request Google's test unit. A production build never carries Google's ids: when `EAS_BUILD_PROFILE` is `production`, `app.config.ts` throws, naming the variable and never the value, if any of the two app ids or four ad unit ids is missing or starts with Google's sample and test publisher `ca-app-pub-3940256099942544`, or if `ADMOB_USE_TEST_IDS` is `true`. To confirm at the first production build: that the config `eas build` reads (locally and on the worker) sees `EAS_BUILD_PROFILE` and the `production` environment's variables; if the local read lacks the variables, the build stops early with a variable's name, which is the intended failure, not a leak.
6. **Unit ids per platform.** `extra.admob.resultsAdUnitId` and `tracksAdUnitId` are `{ android, ios }` objects rather than single strings, because one config serves both platforms and the spec asks for four units.
7. **SDK names to confirm against 17.4.0.** Task 6.17's Step 0 records whether `createForAdRequest` and `useNativeAd` exist, and the names of the request options type, the native ad's `icon.url` field, and the event subscription's `remove()`; Task 6.16 assumes the `AdsConsentDebugGeography` and consent info shapes. Change the card, `useSponsorNativeAd.ts`, `adsConsentClient.ts`, and the shared mock together if a name differs.
8. **The Mobile Ads SDK disclosure.** Which data types Google's disclosure lists for the installed SDK version (Device ID, coarse or approximate location, diagnostics) is an owner check before submission; Task 6.18 writes those rows marked "confirm", and area 8's review notes should match the privacy page's AdMob sentence.
9. **Shapes from other areas.** Aligned with area 4: `ProStatusState` (Task 4.1, `ready` is `{ status: 'ready' } & ProStatus`), `ProSheet`'s props and `ProSheetSource` (Task 4.3, which already includes `'house_card'`), `ProOffer` (Task 4.7) as the signed-in buy flow, `PurchasesState` with `BuyOutcome` unchanged (Task 4.5), and Task 4.2's exact-list case (updated by Task 6.1). A `Pro status error` is treated as hidden (a paying user offline never sees a card; a free user offline sees none either). Remaining gaps: (a) `ProOffer` renders nothing for a guest, so the house card's guest path is area 6's own bare `ProSheet` plus a sign-in redirect (`SponsorProSheetHost`), not an area 4 component; if area 4 later serves guests in `ProOffer`, the host collapses to `ProOffer` alone. (b) Area 4's open question 6 assumes the results-screen footer Pro entry point (`ProSheetSource` `'results'`) belongs to this area; no task in area 6 builds it, and the results card here opens the sheet with `'house_card'` only.
10. **`app/+html.tsx` script line.** Aligned with area 5's Task 5.6: Task 6.11 quotes its import, constant, publisher read, and `{ethicalAdsPublisher === null ? null : <script async src={ETHICAL_ADS_SCRIPT} />}` line, and replaces them with `<EthicalAdsScript />`; the only output change is `async` to `defer`, and area 5's `htmlShell.web.test.tsx` passes unchanged. Whether `expo-constants` resolves `extra` during static rendering is still assumed (area 5 makes the same assumption; if it does not, both files leave the script out).

## Area 7: crawlable pages (`feat/crawlable-pages`)

Risk: standard. Depends on: areas 1 and 2 (all 36 banks under `content/`) and area 5 (`web.output: 'static'`; `ContentProvider` rendering the bundled content before the cache read, Task 5.1; `generateStaticParams` on both menu routes, Task 5.5; `components/seo/PageHead.tsx`, Task 5.6; `scripts/writeHostFiles.mjs`, Task 5.7; the `react-dom/server` polyfill in `jest.setup.ts`, Task 5.2; and the trailing-slash result Task 5.11 Step 2 recorded in the area 5 PR). After launch; nothing else waits on it except area 8's README and handoff lines. Branch: `feat/crawlable-pages`.

What this area assumes from area 5, checked before Task 7.1 starts:

- `state/ContentProvider.tsx` renders its children from the first render (no `return null`), so every static page has a body: `npm run build && grep -c "Step 1 / Select language" dist/index.html` prints 1 or more.
- `components/seo/PageHead.tsx` exports `PageHead({ canonicalPath, description, title })` and `SITE_ORIGIN`, and `PageHead.native.tsx` renders nothing.
- `scripts/writeHostFiles.mjs` exports `writeHostFiles(outputDir)`, run by `npm run build` from the repository root after `expo export`, and `scripts/__tests__/writeHostFiles.test.ts` holds the exact-listing case `writes no .nojekyll and no per-route copies of index.html`.
- The area 5 PR description has a line `Trailing slash: Pages serves /python/ and /python/medium/` or `Trailing slash: Pages serves /python and /python/medium`.

Run `git show origin/main:components/seo/PageHead.tsx`, `git show origin/main:scripts/writeHostFiles.mjs`, and `gh pr view <area 5 PR> --json body --jq .body | grep 'Trailing slash'` first. If an export has another name or signature, use that name in Tasks 7.2 to 7.4 and record the change in the PR description. The tests below are written for the trailing-slash form (`/go/`, `/python/medium/`), which is what Pages is expected to serve for a directory page (`<track>/index.html`). If the recorded line says Pages serves the bare path, the RED author drops the trailing slash from every track and bank path in the tests of Tasks 7.2 to 7.4 (the canonical paths and the expected sitemap locs) before committing, and the implementer drops it from `canonicalPath` and `listTrackPagePaths`.

Design decisions for the area:

- **Where the titles come from.** Only Easy banks are bundled, so the bank pages cannot read Medium and Hard titles from the app bundle. `scripts/buildBankTitles.mjs` reads every bank file under `content/` in Node and writes `services/content/bankTitles.generated.ts`. That module is the only source of the page text.
- **Why `content:build` and not `build`.** The generated module is imported by app code, so `npx tsc --noEmit` and Jest need it committed. `content:build` is the script that regenerates the other committed generated files, and it is the one the CI drift check runs. `build` runs `content:build` first, so the web export always sees fresh titles.
- **Distinct titles.** A bank repeats broad titles: `content/python/easy.json` has 104 questions and 72 distinct titles. A list with repeated lines is thin content, so the index keeps each title once, at its first position. The bank size comes from a separate count.
- **Always rendered.** `TrackSummary` and `BankTitles` render unconditionally, before and after hydration, as secondary content below the interactive step. Search engines index the DOM after running JavaScript, and an ad network's reviewer reads the page in a browser, so text that disappeared on mount would reach neither. Neither route reads a hydration flag: both components read only build-time modules (the bundled manifest and the title index), so the build-time render and the first client render are the same.
- **Titles, descriptions, canonical URLs.** Each track and bank page sets its own title, description, and canonical URL through area 5's `PageHead`, rendered from inside `TrackSummary` and `BankTitles` so the native builds never import the title index. The canonical URL takes the trailing-slash form Task 5.11 recorded, and the sitemap (Task 7.4) uses the same form.
- **Native.** Native builds have no static export to crawl. `TrackSummary.native.tsx` and `BankTitles.native.tsx` render nothing, which keeps the title index out of the native bundles.

`scripts/buildBankTitles.mjs`:

```js
// Build step for the crawlable bank pages: reads every bank the content manifest lists and writes
// services/content/bankTitles.generated.ts with each bank's question count and its distinct
// query.title values in bank order. Titles are written not to give answers away, so they are the
// only question text that leaves the bank files here: never prompts, choices, answers,
// explanations, rationales, or syntax. Runs inside `npm run content:build`, after the manifest.
import { isSafeBankPath } from '@syntactical/content-schema';
import { realpathSync } from 'node:fs';
import { readFile, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

const GENERATED_HEADER = `// GENERATED by scripts/buildBankTitles.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
// Run \`npm run content:build\` to regenerate it.
`;

function listBanks(manifest) {
  return manifest.languages.flatMap((language) =>
    Object.entries(language.banks).map(([difficulty, bank]) => ({
      key: `${language.id}/${difficulty}`,
      path: bank.path,
    })),
  );
}

// Each title once, at its first position: a bank repeats broad titles across questions.
function listDistinctTitles(questions) {
  return [...new Set(questions.map((question) => question.query.title))];
}

async function readBankSummary(contentDir, bankPath) {
  if (!isSafeBankPath(bankPath)) throw new Error(`${bankPath} is not a safe bank path`);
  const bank = JSON.parse(await readFile(join(contentDir, bankPath), 'utf8'));
  return { questionCount: bank.questions.length, titles: listDistinctTitles(bank.questions) };
}

function renderSource(entries) {
  const sorted = [...entries].sort((left, right) => (left.key < right.key ? -1 : 1));
  const countLines = sorted.map(({ key, summary }) => `  ${JSON.stringify(key)}: ${summary.questionCount},`);
  const titleLines = sorted.map(({ key, summary }) => `  ${JSON.stringify(key)}: ${JSON.stringify(summary.titles)},`);
  return `${GENERATED_HEADER}
export const BANK_QUESTION_COUNTS: Readonly<Record<string, number>> = {
${countLines.join('\n')}
};

export const BANK_TITLES: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>> = {
${titleLines.join('\n')}
};
`;
}

export async function buildBankTitles(contentDir, outputPath) {
  const manifest = JSON.parse(await readFile(join(contentDir, 'manifest.json'), 'utf8'));
  const entries = await Promise.all(
    listBanks(manifest).map(async ({ key, path }) => ({ key, summary: await readBankSummary(contentDir, path) })),
  );
  await writeFile(outputPath, renderSource(entries));
  return entries.length;
}

// Compare as file URLs: a plain string compare breaks on a path with a space, and a symlink needs
// its real path.
if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(realpathSync(process.argv[1])).href) {
  const repoDir = process.cwd();
  buildBankTitles(join(repoDir, 'content'), join(repoDir, 'services/content/bankTitles.generated.ts')).catch((err) => {
    console.error(err);
    process.exitCode = 1;
  });
}
```

```tsx
// Crawlable text for one track page of the web build: the track label and tagline, its topics, and each bank's
// question count, below the interactive difficulty step, plus the page's title, description, and canonical URL. The
// route always renders it, before and after hydration, so both the static HTML and the DOM a search engine renders
// carry it. It reads the bundled manifest and the build-time counts, never storage or the network, so the
// build-time render and the first client render match.
import { DIFFICULTIES } from '@syntactical/content-schema';
import { Text, View } from 'react-native';

import { BANK_QUESTION_COUNTS } from '../../services/content/bankTitles.generated';
import { BUNDLED_MANIFEST } from '../../services/content/bundledManifest.generated';
import { findLanguageEntry } from '../../services/content/findLanguageEntry';
import { PageHead } from './PageHead';

type TrackSummaryProps = { language: string };

function describeCount(count: number): string {
  return `${count} ${count === 1 ? 'question' : 'questions'}`;
}

function listBankSizes(language: string, bankIds: readonly string[]) {
  return DIFFICULTIES.filter(({ id }) => bankIds.includes(id)).flatMap(({ id, label }) => {
    const count = BANK_QUESTION_COUNTS[`${language}/${id}`];
    return count === undefined ? [] : [{ count, id, label }];
  });
}

export function TrackSummary({ language }: TrackSummaryProps) {
  const entry = findLanguageEntry(BUNDLED_MANIFEST.languages, language);
  if (!entry) return null;
  const banks = listBankSizes(language, Object.keys(entry.banks));
  return (
    <View className="mt-10 gap-3">
      <PageHead
        canonicalPath={`/${language}/`}
        description={`${entry.label} quiz on Syntactical: ${entry.tagline}`}
        title={`${entry.label} quiz: Easy, Medium, Hard | Syntactical`}
      />
      <Text role="heading" aria-level={2} className="font-mono text-xs uppercase tracking-widest text-muted">
        About {entry.label}
      </Text>
      <Text className="text-sm text-ink">{entry.tagline}</Text>
      {entry.topics.length === 0 ? null : (
        <View role="list" aria-label="Topics" className="gap-1">
          {entry.topics.map(({ id, label }) => (
            <Text key={id} role="listitem" className="text-sm text-muted">
              {label}
            </Text>
          ))}
        </View>
      )}
      <View role="list" aria-label="Banks" className="gap-1">
        {banks.map(({ count, id, label }) => (
          <Text key={id} role="listitem" className="font-mono text-sm text-muted">
            {`${label}: ${describeCount(count)}`}
          </Text>
        ))}
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}
```

`components/seo/BankTitles.tsx`:

```tsx
// Crawlable text for one bank page of the web build: "What this bank covers" and the bank's distinct query titles in
// bank order, below the interactive topic step, plus the page's title, description, and canonical URL. Titles are
// written not to give answers away; no prompt, choice, answer, or explanation is rendered. The route always renders
// it, before and after hydration. It reads the build-time index and the bundled manifest, so Medium and Hard titles
// are there without bundling those banks, and the build-time render and the first client render match.
import { DIFFICULTIES } from '@syntactical/content-schema';
import { Text, View } from 'react-native';

import { BANK_TITLES } from '../../services/content/bankTitles.generated';
import { BUNDLED_MANIFEST } from '../../services/content/bundledManifest.generated';
import { findLanguageEntry } from '../../services/content/findLanguageEntry';
import { PageHead } from './PageHead';

type BankTitlesProps = { difficulty: string; language: string };

// How many titles the page description names before "and more".
const DESCRIBED_TITLE_COUNT = 3;

// Own keys only, so a route segment such as "constructor" never reads the prototype.
function readTitles(key: string): readonly string[] {
  return Object.hasOwn(BANK_TITLES, key) ? BANK_TITLES[key] : [];
}

function describeBank(bankLabel: string, titles: readonly string[]): string {
  const named = titles.slice(0, DESCRIBED_TITLE_COUNT).join(', ');
  const more = titles.length > DESCRIBED_TITLE_COUNT ? ', and more' : '';
  return `${bankLabel} quiz on Syntactical. Covers ${named}${more}.`;
}

export function BankTitles({ difficulty, language }: BankTitlesProps) {
  const titles = readTitles(`${language}/${difficulty}`);
  const languageLabel = findLanguageEntry(BUNDLED_MANIFEST.languages, language)?.label;
  const difficultyLabel = DIFFICULTIES.find(({ id }) => id === difficulty)?.label;
  if (titles.length === 0 || languageLabel === undefined || difficultyLabel === undefined) return null;
  const bankLabel = `${languageLabel} ${difficultyLabel}`;
  return (
    <View className="mt-10 gap-3">
      <PageHead
        canonicalPath={`/${language}/${difficulty}/`}
        description={describeBank(bankLabel, titles)}
        title={`${bankLabel} quiz | Syntactical`}
      />
      <Text role="heading" aria-level={2} className="font-mono text-xs uppercase tracking-widest text-muted">
        What this bank covers
      </Text>
      <View role="list" aria-label="Bank titles" className="gap-1">
        {titles.map((title) => (
          <Text key={title} role="listitem" className="text-sm text-muted">
            {title}
          </Text>
        ))}
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}
```

// The path's segments without the leading and trailing slash: '/python/medium/' is ['python', 'medium'].

`scripts/writeHostFiles.mjs`: change `const { access, copyFile, writeFile } = promises;` to `const { access, copyFile, readFile, readdir, writeFile } = promises;` (`join` is already imported from `node:path`). Then add, above the `writeHostFiles` export:

```js
const SITE_ORIGIN = 'https://syntactical.dev';
// Pages with nothing for a search engine: the admin console and the purchase return page.
const UNLISTED_PAGES = ['admin', 'purchase-complete'];
const ROUTE_FILE = /\.(tsx|ts|jsx|js)$/;
const NON_ROUTE_NAMES = new Set(['_layout', '+not-found', '+html', '__tests__']);

function isDynamicSegment(name) {
  return name.startsWith('[');
}

// Static page paths from the app/ tree, slash-separated, '' for the home page. Dynamic segments
// come from the manifest instead.
async function listStaticPagePaths(dir, prefix = '') {
  const paths = [];
  for (const entry of await readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
    const base = entry.name.replace(ROUTE_FILE, '');
    if (NON_ROUTE_NAMES.has(base) || isDynamicSegment(base)) continue;
    if (entry.isDirectory()) {
      paths.push(...(await listStaticPagePaths(join(dir, entry.name), `${prefix}${entry.name}/`)));
    } else if (ROUTE_FILE.test(entry.name)) {
      paths.push(base === 'index' ? prefix.replace(/\/$/, '') : `${prefix}${base}`);
    }
  }
  return paths;
}

// One page per track and one per bank, each a directory page (<path>/index.html) that Pages serves at a trailing
// slash, the form the area 5 verification recorded and the pages' canonical URLs use. The length and play steps
// take query parameters and are not listed.
function listTrackPagePaths(manifest) {
  return manifest.languages.flatMap((language) => [
    `${language.id}/`,
    ...Object.keys(language.banks)
      .sort()
      .map((difficulty) => `${language.id}/${difficulty}/`),
  ]);
}

function toLoc(path) {
  return `${SITE_ORIGIN}/${path}`;
}

export async function buildSitemap({ appDir = 'app', manifestPath = 'content/manifest.json' } = {}) {
  const manifest = JSON.parse(await readFile(manifestPath, 'utf8'));
  const staticPaths = (await listStaticPagePaths(appDir)).filter((path) => !UNLISTED_PAGES.includes(path)).sort();
  const urls = [...staticPaths, ...listTrackPagePaths(manifest)].map(
    (path) => `  <url><loc>${toLoc(path)}</loc></url>`,
  );
  return `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">
${urls.join('\n')}
</urlset>
`;
}

export function buildRobots() {
  const disallowed = UNLISTED_PAGES.map((page) => `Disallow: /${page}`);
  return ['User-agent: *', ...disallowed, `Sitemap: ${SITE_ORIGIN}/sitemap.xml`, ''].join('\n');
}

export async function writeSitemapFiles(outputDir, options = {}) {
  await writeFile(join(outputDir, 'sitemap.xml'), await buildSitemap(options));
  await writeFile(join(outputDir, 'robots.txt'), buildRobots());
}
```

As the last statement of the exported `writeHostFiles(outputDir)` body, after the `_headers` write, add:

```
Syntactical is a quiz for the parts of a language that behave differently than you expect. Every question bank is free.

Pick a track, then a difficulty. Twelve tracks: Python, Postgres, JavaScript, TypeScript, TypeScript Types, Node.js, Go, Ruby, Rails, SQL, Backend Security, and Frontend Security. Each round is a shuffled pass through a bank of multiple-choice, true/false, and A/B questions about runtime semantics, query planning, coercion, scope, injection, and the sharp edges in between.

Get one wrong and tap Explain. The Query panel shows the syntax, the reasoning, and the tags behind the question, so you learn why the answer is what it is.

What you get
- 12 tracks, each at Easy, Medium, and Hard: 36 question banks, every one free, no account needed.
- A streak, XP, and a daily goal of 10, 20, or 50 XP.
- Review rounds that bring back the questions you missed, on a schedule that spaces them out. They are built on your device, so they work offline.
- Easy banks are on your device from the first launch. Medium and Hard download once and then work offline.
- Signed in, ask about a card after you answer it: 5 a day free, 20 a day with Pro. Signed in, you also get a weekly study note.
- Optional sign-in with an email code, or a password if you set one. Sign in to keep your progress across devices and to restore Pro. Delete your account at any time from Settings.

Syntactical Pro
- Removes the sponsored cards and raises the daily Ask limit from 5 to 20.
- Pro Annual is a subscription that renews every year until you cancel it. Pro Lifetime is a one-time purchase. There is no monthly plan.
- Manage or cancel Pro Annual in your App Store or Google Play account settings. Cancelling keeps Pro until the end of the paid year.

Sponsored cards
Free users see a sponsored card on the results screen from the third round, then every third round, and one in the track list, in the app's own style and labelled Sponsored. Never on a question, never during a round, never in review rounds. The ads are non-personalised: the app does not track you and shows no tracking prompt. Google AdMob receives your device's IP address, from which it may infer an approximate location, to serve and count them.

Your answers and progress stay on your device until you sign in. Usage analytics are anonymous until you sign in, and are never tied to your email. When you ask about a card or get your study note, the card and your question or your week's summary go to Anthropic to write the answer, or to OpenAI when Anthropic is unavailable.

Privacy policy: https://syntactical.dev/privacy
Terms of use: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/dev/stdeula/
```

```
Syntactical is a programming quiz app with 12 tracks (for example Python, Postgres, and Backend Security), each at Easy, Medium, and Hard. Every question bank is free and needs no account.

Syntactical Pro is the only in-app purchase, in two products: syntactical.pro.annual (auto-renewing subscription, one year, in the subscription group "Pro") and syntactical.pro.lifetime (non-consumable). Pro removes the sponsored cards and raises the daily limit of "Ask about this card" from 5 to 20. There is no monthly product.

How to reach Pro:
1. Open the app. The track list shows a card labelled Sponsored between the track groups. When no ad is available it is the house card, "Syntactical Pro", with a See Pro button.
2. Tap See Pro. Or open Settings (reachable from the header on every screen) and tap Go Pro.
3. If you are not signed in, the app sends you to Sign in first. Enter your email, receive a one-time code by email, and enter it. Any email address you control works, and an account is created the first time you sign in.
4. The Syntactical Pro sheet shows two buttons with the store prices, "A year for <price>" and "Forever for <price>", and Not now. Buy either one with your sandbox account.
5. The sponsored cards disappear. Settings shows "Pro until <date>" for the annual product or "Pro, lifetime". Settings, Manage subscription opens the store's subscription page. Settings, Restore purchases restores Pro on a new install.

Sponsored cards: a free user sees one card on the results screen after a round (from the third round, then every third round) and one in the track list. They never appear on a question, during a round, in the query drawer, or in review rounds. On iOS and Android the card is a Google AdMob native ad drawn in the app's own card style, with the "Sponsored" label at the top and the AdChoices icon in the top-right corner. When no ad loads, the card is the house Pro card. Development and preview builds show only Google test ads labelled "Test Ad"; the production build under review requests real ads.

Ads are non-personalised only. The app does not use the advertising identifier for tracking and does not show the App Tracking Transparency prompt. In the EEA and the UK, Google's consent form (User Messaging Platform) appears on first launch, before any ad request; Settings, Privacy settings reopens it.

Account deletion: Settings, then Account, then Delete account. The app asks you to type DELETE to confirm. Deleting removes the account, synced answers, and progress. Records that remain at vendors are limited to analytics events tied to the account's random user id (never the email), the RevenueCat customer record, the email provider's send log, Google AdMob's own ad request records, Anthropic's and OpenAI's records of the questions sent to them under their API retention terms, and the stores' own transactions.

Data collection: email (sign-in); whether the account has Pro and until when; anonymous product analytics through PostHog (no location); a signed-in user's questions about a card and their weekly study note, sent with the card to Anthropic (primary) or to OpenAI (fallback, only when Anthropic is unavailable) to write the answer; and advertising data through Google AdMob on iOS and Android. Google receives the device's IP address, from which it may infer an approximate location, and device information, to serve and count the non-personalised sponsored cards; this data is not linked to the user and not used for tracking. The privacy policy is at https://syntactical.dev/privacy.

Purchases are processed by Apple and Google through RevenueCat. The app never handles card details.
```

**What this area does.** `POST /v1/ask` and `GET /v1/study-note` make one model call each through the `ModelProvider` interface (`server/src/clients/modelProvider.ts`), today Claude Haiku 5.5 only, with the id hard-coded in `server/src/constants/model.ts`. After this area:

- A second provider, OpenAI through the Responses API, answers when the primary fails for a transient reason (timeout, connection, 408, 409, 429, 5xx, or a 400 that does not name the prompt) or a configuration reason (401, 403, 404).
- A refusal, a truncated answer, or a 400 whose error code names the prompt (OpenAI `invalid_prompt`, or a content-policy code) is a decline, not an outage: the provider resolves `null`, the call ends there, no breaker opens, and the learner's message is never sent to the other vendor. Routing a declined learner message to a second vendor would route around the first vendor's refusal, and counting it as a failure would let one learner's crafted message take the primary out of service for everyone.
- One `classifyModelFailure(status, code)` in `server/src/clients/ModelProviderError.ts` decides `config`, `transient`, or `decline` for both providers and for the smoke script.
- A per-process circuit breaker skips a failing provider: three transient failures in a row open it for 60 seconds and log one `warn`; one configuration failure opens it for 15 minutes and logs one `error` naming the provider, the model id, and the status, so a retired model or a rejected parameter is visible at once.
- Model ids come from the environment with today's id as the default, so a model change is a Railway variable change, not a code change.
- A smoke script, type-checked with the rest of the server, runs the real Ask and study-note prompts through each configured provider before a model id changes. Its `--models-only` mode asks each vendor's Models API whether the configured model still exists. A workflow runs the full smoke on demand and the models-only check every day on a schedule, so GitHub tells the owner about a retired model; nothing in the server process checks availability.

**Time budget.** The app waits 30 seconds on these routes (`ASK_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` in `constants/appConfig.ts`, used by `services/studyNote/fetchStudyNote.ts` too) and the code comment in `constants/model.ts` targets about 25. Each attempt gets 11 seconds (the SDK `timeout`) and every SDK client is built with `maxRetries: 0`, because an SDK retry waits out a `retry-after` header first and could push one call past the app's wait while the Ask use stays counted. The failover wrapper owns the retry: it makes at most two attempts, the next provider after a failure or, when only one provider is configured, the same provider once more after a transient failure. It never starts an attempt that could end later than `CALL_TIMEOUT_MS` (22 seconds, twice the attempt timeout) after the call started, so the whole call is bounded at 22 seconds, as today's 12-second budget with one SDK retry targeted 24.

**Global constraints for this area.**

- Provider ids: `'anthropic' | 'openai'`. `MODEL_PRIMARY` defaults to `anthropic`.
- `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` defaults to `claude-haiku-5-5` and must match `^claude-[a-z0-9-]+$`. `OPENAI_MODEL` is required when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set and has no default; the owner chooses a small, fast model. `OPENAI_REASONING_EFFORT` is optional (`low | medium | high`) and the `reasoning` field is omitted when it is unset, so a non-reasoning model is never sent a parameter it rejects.
- Model constants: `ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS = 11_000`, `CALL_TIMEOUT_MS = 22_000`, `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 2`, `SDK_RETRIES = 0`. Breaker: `FAILURES_TO_OPEN = 3`, `TRANSIENT_COOLDOWN_MS = 60_000`, `CONFIG_COOLDOWN_MS = 900_000`.
- Failure classes: 401, 403, 404 are `config`; a 400 whose code is in `DECLINE_CODES` (`invalid_prompt`, `content_policy_violation`) is `decline`; any other 400, 408, 409, 429, 5xx, a connection error or timeout, and any non-SDK error are `transient`.
- Logging: provider, model id, outcome (`answered | declined | transient | config`), latency in milliseconds, and whether the answer came from the secondary. One `warn` per transient breaker opening, one `error` per config opening. Never the prompt, the learner's message, the answer text, or an SDK error object (the existing routes already avoid logging the error object for this reason).
- No change to the routes' responses: both still answer 503 `ASK_UNAVAILABLE` or `STUDY_NOTE_UNAVAILABLE` when no provider answers, and Ask still hands back the reserved use.

Commands for this area: unit tests `cd server && npx vitest run <path>`; integration tests `cd server && npx vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts <path>` (needs `TEST_DATABASE_URL` or local Docker); GREEN gate `cd server && npm test && npm run test:integration && npm run typecheck`, then `npm run lint` at the root. Task 9.8 also runs the root Jest suite and `npx tsc --noEmit` for the app.

`server/src/clients/ModelProviderError.ts`:

```ts
// A failed model request, classified once for both providers, the failover, and the smoke script.
// `config` means the request cannot succeed until the configuration changes (a retired model, a
// bad key, a forbidden request); `decline` means the vendor refused this prompt, which is final
// and is never sent to the other vendor, so the provider resolves null instead of throwing;
// `transient` means it may succeed on retry. The error is built from the provider, model, status,
// and kind only: the SDK error is dropped because its request carries the learner's message.
type ProviderId = 'anthropic' | 'openai';
type ModelFailureOutcome = 'config' | 'decline' | 'transient';
type ModelFailureKind = Exclude<ModelFailureOutcome, 'decline'>;

const CONFIG_STATUSES = new Set([401, 403, 404]);
// Error codes a vendor sends with a 400 when the prompt itself is refused. OpenAI's Responses API
// answers a prompt its usage-policy screen flags with `invalid_prompt`.
const DECLINE_CODES = new Set(['content_policy_violation', 'invalid_prompt']);

function classifyModelFailure(status: number | null, code: string | null): ModelFailureOutcome {
  if (status !== null && CONFIG_STATUSES.has(status)) return 'config';
  if (status === 400 && code !== null && DECLINE_CODES.has(code)) return 'decline';
  return 'transient';
}

class ModelProviderError extends Error {
  readonly kind: ModelFailureKind;
  readonly model: string;
  readonly provider: ProviderId;
  readonly status: number | null;

  constructor(provider: ProviderId, model: string, status: number | null, kind: ModelFailureKind) {
    super(`${provider} ${model} failed (${kind}${status === null ? '' : `, ${status}`})`);
    this.name = 'ModelProviderError';
    this.kind = kind;
    this.model = model;
    this.provider = provider;
    this.status = status;
  }
}

export { classifyModelFailure, ModelProviderError };
export type { ModelFailureKind, ModelFailureOutcome, ProviderId };
```

```

- Result: the joined `output_text` items of the response's message output, trimmed; `null` when `status` is not `completed`, when any message content item is a `refusal`, or when the text is empty. ```ts
// The OpenAI fallback behind POST /v1/ask and GET /v1/study-note, behind the same interface as the
// Claude provider. One Responses API request per answer, with SDK retries off (the failover
// retries). Resolves the answer text, or null on a refusal, an incomplete response, an empty
// answer, or a 400 that flags the prompt, so a partial answer is never shown and a refused prompt
// is final. Rejects with a ModelProviderError; the SDK error is dropped because its request carries
// the learner's message. The key comes from the caller; this module never reads the environment.
import OpenAI from 'openai';
import type { ClientOptions } from 'openai';

import { MODEL } from '../constants/model.js';

import { classifyModelFailure, ModelProviderError } from './ModelProviderError.js';
import type { ModelProvider } from './modelProvider.js';

type ResponsesClient = Pick<OpenAI['responses'], 'create'>;

interface OpenAIProviderDeps {
  apiKey: string;
  model: string;
  reasoningEffort?: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high';
  // Test seam: replaces the SDK's responses resource.
  responses?: ResponsesClient;
}

function buildOpenAIOptions(apiKey: string): ClientOptions {
  return { apiKey, maxRetries: MODEL.SDK_RETRIES, timeout: MODEL.ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS };
}

function readAnswer(response: OpenAI.Responses.Response): string | null {
  if (response.status !== 'completed') return null;
  const parts: string[] = [];
  for (const item of response.output) {
    if (item.type !== 'message') continue;
    for (const content of item.content) {
      if (content.type === 'refusal') return null;
      if (content.type === 'output_text') parts.push(content.text);
    }
  }
  const text = parts.join('').trim();
  return text === '' ? null : text;
}

function createOpenAIModelProvider({ apiKey, model, reasoningEffort, responses }: OpenAIProviderDeps) {
  const client = responses ?? new OpenAI(buildOpenAIOptions(apiKey)).responses;
  const provider: ModelProvider = {
    id: 'openai',
    model,
    async answer({ system, user }) {
      let response: OpenAI.Responses.Response;
      try {
        response = await client.create({
          input: user,
          instructions: system,
          max_output_tokens: MODEL.MAX_TOKENS,
          model,
          ...(reasoningEffort ? { reasoning: { effort: reasoningEffort } } : {}),
        });
      } catch (error) {
        const isApiError = error instanceof OpenAI.APIError;
        const status = isApiError ? (error.status ?? null) : null;
        const outcome = classifyModelFailure(status, isApiError ? (error.code ?? null) : null);
        if (outcome === 'decline') return null;
        throw new ModelProviderError('openai', model, status, outcome);
      }
      return readAnswer(response);
    },
  };
  return provider;
}

export { buildOpenAIOptions, createOpenAIModelProvider };
export type { ResponsesClient };
```

### Task 9.4: failover provider with a circuit breaker and the one retry

**Files:**

- Create: `server/src/clients/failoverModelProvider.ts`
- Test: `server/src/__tests__/clients/failoverModelProvider.test.ts` (new)

**Interfaces:**

- Produces: `createFailoverModelProvider({ providers: ModelProvider[], logger: Logger, now?: () => number }): ModelProvider`. `providers[0]` is the primary. `id` and `model` of the returned provider are the primary's.
- Order: try the providers whose breaker is closed, in order; when every breaker is open, try the primary anyway, so an outage of both still gets an attempt. With one provider configured, the same provider is tried a second time after a transient failure (never after a config failure). At most `MODEL.MAX_ATTEMPTS` (2) attempts per call, and no attempt starts when `now() + ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS` would pass `callStart + CALL_TIMEOUT_MS`, so the call is bounded at 22 seconds given the SDK's 11-second attempt timeout.
- Outcomes: a resolved value, `null` included, ends the call: a decline is never retried or sent elsewhere, and it records no failure. A rejection records a failure for that provider and moves on; when the attempts run out, rethrow the last `ModelProviderError`. A non-`ModelProviderError` rejection counts as transient. A success resets the provider's failure count and closes its breaker.
- Breaker: three consecutive transient failures open it for `TRANSIENT_COOLDOWN_MS` and log `warn` `{ cooldownMs, model, provider }`, message `model provider skipped after repeated failures`, once per opening. One config failure opens it for `CONFIG_COOLDOWN_MS` and logs `error` `{ model, provider, status }` once per opening. A 400 that is not a decline is transient (Task 9.2), so one such request never opens the config breaker.
- Logs one `info` line per attempt: `{ provider, model, outcome, latencyMs, isFailover }`, message `model call`. Never the prompt or the answer.

// server/src/__tests__/clients/failoverModelProvider.test.ts
// The failover in front of the model providers: the primary answers when it can; a failure moves the
// call to the next provider, or retries the only one once; a decline is final, including an OpenAI
// 400 that flags the prompt; a failing provider is skipped for a cooldown and the opening is logged;
// a configuration failure (a retired model, a bad key) opens a long cooldown and logs an error; the
// whole call is bounded at twice the attempt timeout. The log never carries the prompt or the answer.
import OpenAI from 'openai';
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

import { createFailoverModelProvider } from '../../clients/failoverModelProvider.js';
import { classifyModelFailure, ModelProviderError } from '../../clients/ModelProviderError.js';
import type { ProviderId } from '../../clients/ModelProviderError.js';
import type { ModelProvider } from '../../clients/modelProvider.js';
import { createOpenAIModelProvider } from '../../clients/openAIModelProvider.js';
import type { ResponsesClient } from '../../clients/openAIModelProvider.js';
import { MODEL } from '../../constants/model.js';

import { createRecordingLogger } from '../support/recordingLogger.js';

const PROMPT = { system: 'You are the tutor.', user: '<learner_message>"secret question"</learner_message>' };

type Outcome = string | null | 'transient' | 'config' | 'bad-request';

interface FakeClock {
  advance(ms: number): void;
  now(): number;
}

function fakeClock(): FakeClock {
  let value = 0;
  return {
    advance: (ms) => {
      value += ms;
    },
    now: () => value,
  };
}

// A provider that plays its outcomes in order and repeats the last; each call moves the clock by
// latencyMs, standing in for the time the request took.
function provider(
  id: ProviderId,
  outcomes: Outcome[],
  timing: { clock?: FakeClock; latencyMs?: number } = {},
): ModelProvider & { calls: number } {
  const queue = [...outcomes];
  const model = `${id}-model`;
  const fake = {
    calls: 0,
    id,
    model,
    answer: vi.fn(() => {
      fake.calls += 1;
      timing.clock?.advance(timing.latencyMs ?? 0);
      const next = queue.length > 1 ? queue.shift() : queue[0];
      if (next === 'transient') return Promise.reject(new ModelProviderError(id, model, 503, 'transient'));
      if (next === 'config') return Promise.reject(new ModelProviderError(id, model, 404, 'config'));
      if (next === 'bad-request') {
        const kind = classifyModelFailure(400, null);
        if (kind === 'decline') throw new Error('a 400 without a policy code must not be a decline');
        return Promise.reject(new ModelProviderError(id, model, 400, kind));
      }
      return Promise.resolve(next ?? null);
    }),
  };
  return fake;
}

function levels(entries: Array<Record<string, unknown>>, level: string) {
  return entries.filter((entry) => entry.level === level);
}

describe('createFailoverModelProvider', () => {
  it('answers from the primary and never calls the secondary', async () => {
    const primary = provider('anthropic', ['From Claude.']);
    const secondary = provider('openai', ['From OpenAI.']);
    const { logger } = createRecordingLogger();

    await expect(createFailoverModelProvider({ logger, providers: [primary, secondary] }).answer(PROMPT)).resolves.toBe(
      'From Claude.',
    );
    expect(secondary.calls).toBe(0);
  });

  it('answers from the secondary when the primary fails, without retrying the primary', async () => {
    const primary = provider('anthropic', ['transient']);
    const secondary = provider('openai', ['From OpenAI.']);
    const { logger } = createRecordingLogger();

    await expect(createFailoverModelProvider({ logger, providers: [primary, secondary] }).answer(PROMPT)).resolves.toBe(
      'From OpenAI.',
    );
    expect(primary.calls).toBe(1);
  });

  it('treats a decline as final and never sends it to the secondary', async () => {
    const primary = provider('anthropic', [null]);
    const secondary = provider('openai', ['From OpenAI.']);
    const { logger } = createRecordingLogger();

    await expect(
      createFailoverModelProvider({ logger, providers: [primary, secondary] }).answer(PROMPT),
    ).resolves.toBeNull();
    expect(secondary.calls).toBe(0);

  it('resolves null for an OpenAI 400 invalid_prompt, never calls the secondary, and opens no breaker', async () => {
    const error = OpenAI.APIError.generate(

```ts
// The model providers in order, behind one ModelProvider. The first provider whose breaker is
// closed answers; a failure moves the call to the next, or, with one provider configured, retries
// it once (the SDKs never retry, so this is the only retry). At most two attempts, and none that
// could end after CALL_TIMEOUT_MS. A decline (null) is final, because a refusal is an answer and
// is never routed to another vendor. A provider that fails three times in a row is skipped for a
// minute (one warning); one configuration failure (a retired model, a bad key) skips it for 15
// minutes (one error). When every breaker is open the primary is tried anyway. State is per
// process, as the rate limiter's is.
import type { Logger } from 'pino';

import { MODEL } from '../constants/model.js';

import { ModelProviderError } from './ModelProviderError.js';
import type { ModelFailureKind, ProviderId } from './ModelProviderError.js';
import type { ModelPrompt, ModelProvider } from './modelProvider.js';

const { ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS, CALL_TIMEOUT_MS, MAX_ATTEMPTS } = MODEL;
const { CONFIG_COOLDOWN_MS, FAILURES_TO_OPEN, TRANSIENT_COOLDOWN_MS } = MODEL.BREAKER;

interface BreakerState {
  failures: number;
  openUntil: number;
}

interface FailoverDeps {
  logger: Logger;
  now?: () => number;
  providers: ModelProvider[];
}

function toFailure(provider: ModelProvider, error: unknown): ModelProviderError {
  return error instanceof ModelProviderError
    ? error
    : new ModelProviderError(provider.id, provider.model, null, 'transient');
}

function createFailoverModelProvider({ logger, now = Date.now, providers }: FailoverDeps): ModelProvider {
  const [primary] = providers;
  if (primary === undefined) throw new Error('createFailoverModelProvider needs at least one provider');
  const breakers = new Map<ProviderId, BreakerState>(providers.map(({ id }) => [id, { failures: 0, openUntil: 0 }]));

  function isOpen(id: ProviderId): boolean {
    return (breakers.get(id)?.openUntil ?? 0) > now();
  }

  function openBreaker(state: BreakerState, kind: ModelFailureKind): void {
    state.openUntil = now() + (kind === 'config' ? CONFIG_COOLDOWN_MS : TRANSIENT_COOLDOWN_MS);
    state.failures = 0;
  }

  function recordFailure(failure: ModelProviderError): void {
    const state = breakers.get(failure.provider);
    if (state === undefined) return;
    const { model, provider, status } = failure;
    if (failure.kind === 'config') {
      const wasOpen = isOpen(provider);
      openBreaker(state, 'config');
      if (!wasOpen)
        logger.error({ model, provider, status }, 'model configuration failure; provider skipped for 15 minutes');
      return;
    }
    state.failures += 1;
    if (state.failures >= FAILURES_TO_OPEN) {
      openBreaker(state, 'transient');
      logger.warn(
        { cooldownMs: TRANSIENT_COOLDOWN_MS, model, provider },
        'model provider skipped after repeated failures',
      );
    }
  }

  function recordSuccess(id: ProviderId): void {
    const state = breakers.get(id);
    if (state !== undefined) Object.assign(state, { failures: 0, openUntil: 0 });
  }

  // With one provider configured the wrapper is its retry; otherwise the next provider is.
  function plan(): ModelProvider[] {
    if (providers.length === 1) return [primary, primary];
    const ready = providers.filter(({ id }) => !isOpen(id));
    return ready.length > 0 ? ready : [primary];
  }

  async function answer(prompt: ModelPrompt): Promise<string | null> {
    const callStarted = now();
    let lastFailure: ModelProviderError | undefined;
    for (const [index, candidate] of plan().slice(0, MAX_ATTEMPTS).entries()) {
      if (index > 0 && now() + ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS > callStarted + CALL_TIMEOUT_MS) break;
      if (lastFailure?.kind === 'config' && lastFailure.provider === candidate.id) break;
      const started = now();
      const base = { isFailover: candidate.id !== primary.id, model: candidate.model, provider: candidate.id };
      try {
        const result = await candidate.answer(prompt);
        recordSuccess(candidate.id);
        logger.info(
          { ...base, latencyMs: now() - started, outcome: result === null ? 'declined' : 'answered' },
          'model call',
        );
        return result;
      } catch (error) {
        lastFailure = toFailure(candidate, error);
        recordFailure(lastFailure);
        logger.info({ ...base, latencyMs: now() - started, outcome: lastFailure.kind }, 'model call');
      }
    }
    throw lastFailure;
  }

  return { answer, id: primary.id, model: primary.model };
}

export { createFailoverModelProvider };
```

describe('with a fallback provider', () => {
  const silentLogger = pino({ level: 'silent' });

  it('answers from the secondary when the primary is down and counts one use', async () => {
    const signed = await signIn(
      createFailoverModelProvider({
        logger: silentLogger,

      createFailoverModelProvider({

        providers: [

          createFakeModelProvider({ failure: 'transient', id: 'openai' }),

      }),
    );

});

### Task 9.7: model smoke script and its daily model check

No behaviour to unit-test: the script calls the real APIs. Its parts that can drift are typed and reused: the environment rules (`loadEnv`, `listConfiguredModels` from Task 9.5), the providers (Tasks 9.2 and 9.3), the SDK options (`buildAnthropicOptions`, `buildOpenAIOptions`), the failure classifier (Task 9.2), and the tested prompt builders. The script lives under `server/src`, so `npm run typecheck -w server` (which the root `typecheck:workspaces` and CI run) checks it against those signatures; `server/tsconfig.json` includes only `src`, and `tsx` strips types without checking them, so a script outside `src` could rot unnoticed until the day it is needed.

Model availability is checked here, not in the server process. A retired model answers 404 at once, so the first learner who meets it gets a fast failover to the secondary (Task 9.4) and the server logs the config error then; what a daily check adds is a signal during quiet hours, which a scheduled workflow gives without boot-time network calls or timers in `startServer`.

**Files:**

- Create: `server/src/scripts/modelSmoke.ts`
- Modify: `server/package.json` (`"model:smoke": "tsx src/scripts/modelSmoke.ts"`; `tsx` is already a root dev dependency)
- Modify: `server/tsconfig.build.json` (add `"src/scripts"` to `exclude`, beside `"src/__tests__"` and `"src/testing"`, so the script does not ship in `dist`)
- Create: `.github/workflows/model-smoke.yml`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the script**

`server/src/scripts/modelSmoke.ts`:

- Environment: copy `process.env`, delete every variable whose value is the empty string (GitHub passes an unset secret or variable as `''`, which `OPENAI_API_KEY: z.string().trim().min(1)` rejects), set `ALLOW_STUBBED_INTEGRATIONS=true` and a placeholder `DATABASE_URL` when they are missing, and parse with `loadEnv`. It never connects to a database. `listConfiguredModels(env)` names the providers to check; `--provider anthropic|openai` narrows it to one.
- Default mode: read three fixed questions from `content/python/easy.json`, `content/postgres/medium.json`, and `content/javascript/hard.json` through `readServerQuestions`, build one Ask prompt per question with `buildAskPrompt` and one study-note prompt from a fixed synthetic summary with `buildStudyNotePrompt`, and send all four to each configured provider separately (built with `createAnthropicModelProvider` or `createOpenAIModelProvider`, not through the failover), printing one line per call: provider, model, outcome (`answered`, `declined`, `transient`, `config`), latency, and the first 80 characters of the answer. Exit 1 when any call rejects or declines, so a model change that breaks the prompts fails loudly. With no key: print `No model key is set` and exit 1.
- `--models-only` mode: for each configured provider, call `new Anthropic(buildAnthropicOptions({ apiKey, workspaceId })).models.retrieve(model)` or `new OpenAI(buildOpenAIOptions(apiKey)).models.retrieve(model)` (both SDKs expose `models.retrieve`; the Anthropic Models API is `client.models.retrieve(id)` in the Claude API reference). Print one line per provider: provider, model, and `available`, or the status and `classifyModelFailure(status, null)`. Exit 1 when any result is `config`: a 404 (the model is retired or misspelled), or a 401 or 403 (the key no longer works). A `transient` result (a vendor outage) prints its line and does not fail the run. With no key: print `No model key is set; nothing to check` and exit 0, so the schedule stays green before the owner adds keys.
- Never print a key, a prompt, or an SDK error object; print the status only.

```md
## Changing or losing a model

Ask and the study note call `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` (default `claude-haiku-5-5`) first, or `OPENAI_MODEL` first when
`MODEL_PRIMARY=openai`. When both keys are set, a failure on the first provider moves the call to the second; with
one key, the server retries that provider once. A prompt the vendor refuses is final and is never sent to the other
vendor.

To switch a model (an upgrade, or a retirement notice from Anthropic or OpenAI):

1. Run `npm run model:smoke -w server` locally with the new id in `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` or `OPENAI_MODEL`, or run the
   "Model smoke" workflow with the id as its input. Every line must say `answered`.
2. Set the variable on the staging Railway service, ask one question in a preview build, and check the
   `model call` log lines show the new id with outcome `answered`.
3. Set it on production, and set the repository variable of the same name (Settings, Secrets and variables,
   Actions, Variables) so the daily check tests the model production uses.

The "Model smoke" workflow also runs every day with `--models-only` and fails when a configured model is gone (404)
or a key is refused (401, 403); GitHub emails you about the failed run. If a model is retired or a parameter is
rejected before you switch, the server logs `model configuration failure` with the provider, model, and status,
skips that provider for 15 minutes, and answers from the other one. After three failures in a row it logs
`model provider skipped after repeated failures` and skips the provider for a minute. With only one key set, Ask
and the study note answer 503 until the variable is fixed.
```

| One failure classifier for both providers and the smoke script                                                     | 9.2, 9.3, 9.7      |
| A failing provider is skipped for a cooldown with one warning; a configuration failure for longer, with one error  | 9.4                |
